records.title: Defining the optimal duration of remote home tonometry for accurate characterization of intraocular pressure fluctuation.

content.title: Defining the optimal duration of remote home tonometry for accurate characterization of intraocular pressure fluctuation.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To determine the minimal duration of remote intraocular pressure (IOP) monitoring needed to yield accurate IOP fluctuation metrics in patients.

Design

Secondary modeling analysis of retrospective data, validated with a large national database.

Participants

397 patients from the Moran Eye Center and/or Wilmer Eye Institute and 1,579 patients from a MyEyes CorporationTM database who utilized an iCare HOME/HOME2 tonometer and recorded ≥3 measurements throughout each day over several consecutive days.

Methods

Bootstrapped progressive day-censorship analyses and exponential decay modeling were used to estimate the number of monitoring days required to achieve 95% of the maximal model-based reduction in error for IOP metrics, including mean, maximum, range, and standard deviation (SD). Ground truth for each metric was defined using all available measurements within each eye-specific monitoring period. Sensitivity analyses assessing the effects of diagnosis, treatment, and three daily IOP measurements were also completed.

Main outcome measures

Mean absolute error (MAE) and mean relative error (MRE) for IOP mean, maximum, range, and SD; the number of monitoring days required to achieve 95% of the maximal model-based reduction in error.

Results

Across both datasets, approximately 6-7 monitoring days were required to achieve 95% of the modeled reduction in error for daily mean, maximum, range, and SD of IOP in the primary analysis. Sensitivity analyses demonstrated longer monitoring requirements in primary open-angle glaucoma (9.1-10.0 days) compared with glaucoma suspects (5.5-6.7 days), secondary open-angle glaucoma (6.4-8.0 days), and primary angle-closure glaucoma (7.8-8.3 days). Monitoring durations remained relatively consistent before and after selective laser trabeculoplasty (8.4-9.0 days) and Hydrus microstent implantation (6.0-6.8 days). Restricting measurements to only three daily IOP recordings throughout the day extended monitoring duration to approximately 10 days in the Moran/Wilmer dataset and longer in the MyEyes dataset. Additionally, 74.1% of peak IOP measurements occurred outside typical clinic hours.

Conclusions

Remote tonometry provides clinically meaningful characterization of IOP metrics beyond traditional office-based measurements. Depending on the clinical context, seven to ten consecutive monitoring days consisting of measurements across each day are needed to represent a patient's true IOP pattern.

records.title: Impact of corneal microbial latency detected by metagenomic next-generation sequencing on postoperative recovery after keratorefractive lenticule extraction.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Impact of corneal microbial latency detected by metagenomic next-generation sequencing on postoperative recovery after keratorefractive lenticule extraction.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To investigate the microbial species latent in corneas of healthy individuals and determine whether small-incision lenticule extraction (SMILE) serves as a risk factor for pathogen reactivation.

Setting

Ophthalmology Department of Peking University Third Hospital, Beijing, China.

Design

Prospective cohort study.

Methods

Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) was used to analyze the microbial composition of corneal lenticules from SMILE. Based on the results, patients were categorized into viral group (VG) and nonviral pathogen group (NVPG). 2 Matched groups (MG1 and MG2) were established by selecting pathogen-negative individuals at a 1:4 ratio relative to 2 positive groups. Using SPSS to analyze baseline characteristics, preoperative ocular parameters, and postoperative ocular parameters among groups.

Results

Among the detected pathogens, latent Herpesviruses were identified in 9 cases (4.31%), Papillomavirus were 4 cases (1.91%), and nonviral pathogens were 20 cases (9.57%). Both VG and NVPG groups showed no significant differences in baseline characteristics or preoperative ocular parameters compared with MG groups. In postoperative ocular parameters, no significant differences were found between VG and MG1, although intergroup variations in intraocular pressure and corneal thickness were observed ( P > .05). However, NVPG demonstrated significantly poorer results than MG2 in 1-month spherical equivalent ( P = .033) and corneal epithelial staining ( P = .044).

Conclusions

These findings indicate pathogen latency does not affect ocular status and SMILE surgery is unlikely to reactivate latent viruses or exerts minimal influence. Viral latency has almost no impact on postoperative recovery, while latent nonviral pathogens may interfere with postoperative recovery.

records.title: External validation of a deep-learning algorithm for perimetric glaucoma detection on color fundus photographs in the Rotterdam Study.

content.title: External validation of a deep-learning algorithm for perimetric glaucoma detection on color fundus photographs in the Rotterdam Study.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To externally validate a deep-learning (DL) algorithm detecting perimetric glaucoma on color fundus photographs (CFPs) in a population-based cohort.

Design

External validation in a prospective population-based cohort.

Participants

Participants aged 50-80 years from three Rotterdam Study cohorts.

Methods

We applied the winning Artificial Intelligence for Robust Glaucoma Screening (AIROGS) challenge algorithm, trained on 101,442 macula-centered CFPs to detect referable presumed perimetric glaucoma. Performance was assessed at eye and participant level, with participant-level cluster bootstrap confidence intervals. Misclassified cases underwent qualitative review. Longitudinal detection was evaluated by Kaplan-Meier analysis. Additionally, paired analyses compared macula- with disc-centered CFPs. A post-hoc analysis examined the effect of image quality on positive predictive value (PPV).

Main outcome measures

Sensitivity at 95% specificity, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC), partial AUC (pAUC) for 90-100% specificity, PPV, and precision-recall AUC (PR-AUC).

Results

Among 19,088 eyes (9,837 participants), 201 eyes (1.1%) had perimetric glaucoma. At eye level, sensitivity at 95% specificity was 70.6% (95% CI: 63.8-76.8), with an ROC-AUC of 0.911 (95% CI: 0.887-0.934) and a PR-AUC of 0.343 (95% CI: 0.274-0.427). At participant level, sensitivity was 68.8% (95% CI: 61.8-75.9) and ROC-AUC 0.909 (95% CI: 0.882-0.934). Overall, this resulted in 5.1 referrals per detected glaucoma case. True positives showed more advanced visual field damage than false negatives (median mean deviation -10.8 vs -5.8 dB; P < 0.001). Among true positives with prior imaging, 33 of 61 (54%) were flagged before conversion, typically 4-7 years before diagnosis. Discrimination in the 90-100% specificity range was higher for disc- than macula-centered CFPs (pAUC 0.860 vs 0.802; P = 0.003). PPV improved substantially after excluding CFPs with incomplete optic nerve head (ONH) visibility.

Conclusions

The DL-algorithm achieved meaningful discrimination for perimetric glaucoma in an external population-based dataset. Correctly identified cases were frequently flagged at an earlier examination, years before the perimetric diagnosis. Despite having been trained exclusively on macula-centered CFPs, the DL-algorithm showed no loss of discriminative performance on disc-centered CFPs. Incomplete ONH visibility was an important source of false positives. These findings support CFP-based deep learning as a scalable triage tool for glaucoma screening and highlight image acquisition standards for implementation.

records.title: Clinical and refractive outcomes of secondary intraocular lens fixation using small-incision scleral suture fixation vs intrascleral haptic fixation.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Clinical and refractive outcomes of secondary intraocular lens fixation using small-incision scleral suture fixation vs intrascleral haptic fixation.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare clinical and refractive outcomes of small-incision scleral suture fixation (SSF) vs intrascleral haptic fixation (ISHF) for secondary intraocular lens (IOL) implantation in adults.

Setting

Single outpatient ophthalmology clinic.

Design

Retrospective, single-center cohort study.

Methods

Eyes undergoing small-incision SSF or ISHF between 2019 and 2024 were identified. Demographics, surgical indications, IOL types, refractive accuracy, and postoperative complications were analyzed. Refractive outcomes were evaluated using spherical equivalent refractive accuracy (SERA) and absolute SERA (ASERA).

Results

132 eyes from 125 adult patients were included. 56 eyes underwent SSF, and 76 underwent ISHF. Indications included subluxated IOL (58%), dislocated IOL (17%), aphakia (20%), and uveitis-glaucoma-hyphema syndrome (5%). In the SSF group, MX60E or ET IOLs predominated, while CT Lucia 602 was most common in ISHF. Mean SERA was -0.45 diopters (D) for SSF and -0.36 D for ISHF ( P = .48); mean ASERA was 0.52 D and 0.54 D, respectively ( P = .96). At postoperative month 3, 70% of SSF vs 62% of ISHF eyes were within ±0.50 D of target and 85% vs 86% were within ±1.00 D. Complication rates were low and comparable, with trends toward higher early hypotony in SSF and more reoperations in ISHF.

Conclusions

Both small-incision SSF and ISHF are safe and effective for secondary IOL implantation in adults. Refractive outcomes were comparable, with SSF demonstrating slightly greater predictability and fewer reoperations, while ISHF was associated with less early hypotony. Technique selection should be guided by surgeon experience, IOL choice, and patient-specific factors.

records.title: Submacular Hemorrhage Requiring Procedural Intervention During Anti-VEGF Therapy for Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration in Japan: The JTY Three-Center Real-World Incidence Study.

content.title: Submacular Hemorrhage Requiring Procedural Intervention During Anti-VEGF Therapy for Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration in Japan: The JTY Three-Center Real-World Incidence Study.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To estimate the incidence and clinical characteristics of submacular hemorrhage (SMH) requiring procedural intervention during anti-VEGF therapy for neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) in a Japanese multicenter real-world setting, with exploratory comparison according to the preceding anti-VEGF agent.

Methods

This multicenter retrospective real-world incidence study reviewed surgical records from three Japanese centers to identify SMH requiring gas injection or vitrectomy during ongoing anti-VEGF treatment. The denominator was the total number of anti-VEGF injections for nAMD during the same period. Incidence per 1,000 injections and site-adjusted incidence rate ratios (IRRs) were estimated using quasi-Poisson regression.

Results

Among 47,358 injections, 54 SMH events requiring procedural intervention were identified (1.14 per 1,000 injections). Median final BCVA after procedural treatment was 1.00 logMAR (Snellen equivalent, 20/200), compared with 0.46 logMAR before SMH (approximately 20/60). PCV accounted for 39 events (72.2%), and prior SMH was documented in 12 eyes (22.2%). Crude incidence was 2.20 for ranibizumab, 1.09 for brolucizumab, 1.08 for aflibercept, and 0.24 for faricimab. Using aflibercept as the reference, IRRs were 1.83 for ranibizumab (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.73-4.59; P = 0.195), 0.91 for brolucizumab (95% CI, 0.25-3.28; P = 0.883), and 0.20 for faricimab (95% CI, 0.01-3.16; P = 0.251).

Conclusions

SMH requiring procedural intervention during anti-VEGF therapy for nAMD was uncommon but visually severe; among affected eyes, PCV accounted for 72.2% of events. Exploratory drug-specific analyses did not demonstrate significant adjusted differences among anti-VEGF agents. Future patient-level studies should evaluate subtype-specific incidence, hemorrhagic recurrence, and polyp-directed treatment strategies in PCV-rich populations.

records.title: PREDICTIVE OPTICAL COHERENCE TOMOGRAPHY BIOMARKERS OF RETINAL CHANGES AND VISUAL OUTCOMES IN SILICONE OIL ENDOTAMPONADE IDENTIFIED BY ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE.

content.title: PREDICTIVE OPTICAL COHERENCE TOMOGRAPHY BIOMARKERS OF RETINAL CHANGES AND VISUAL OUTCOMES IN SILICONE OIL ENDOTAMPONADE IDENTIFIED BY ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To quantify retinal layer changes and visual outcomes in eyes with silicone oil (SO) endotamponade for rhegmatogenous retinal detachment using optical coherence tomography (OCT) biomarkers and prediction models.

Methods

Seventy-six eyes with SO endotamponade underwent macular volume OCT at SO insertion and just before SO removal. An automated segmentation tool quantified retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL), ganglion cell layer + inner plexiform layer (GCL + IPL), other retinal layers, and fluid (subretinal fluid, intraretinal fluid). Eyes with and without macular edema (ME) during tamponade were compared. A random forest classifier explored predictors of categorical best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) change (improved, stable, worsened).

Results

RNFL and GCL + IPL thinned significantly during tamponade (RNFL 35.4 ± 18.1 µ m to 26.9 ± 19.1 µ m; GCL + IPL 74.7 ± 17.4 µ m to 55.8 ± 27.2 µ m), whereas photoreceptor (PR)+retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) showed mild thickening (59.6 ± 12.6 µ m to 61.4 ± 15.0 µ m). Other layers and fluid compartments showed no clinically relevant change. Macular edema occurred in 44/76 eyes (57.9%), but retinal layer changes and BCVA outcomes (improved/stable/worsened) were similar in ME and non-ME groups (χ 2P = 0.94). In the prediction model, RNFL, GCL + IPL, and PR+RPE were the strongest contributors, whereas SO duration and ME status had minimal impact.

Conclusion

SO endotamponade was associated with selective inner retinal thinning and mild PR+RPE thickening. Postoperative visual recovery depended mainly on inner retinal integrity, supporting OCT-derived layer biomarkers as practical tools for prognostication after SO removal.

records.title: Serum Ang-1, sFLT-1, and sST2 Profiles Distinguish Anti-VEGF Responders in Diabetic Macular Edema.

content.title: Serum Ang-1, sFLT-1, and sST2 Profiles Distinguish Anti-VEGF Responders in Diabetic Macular Edema.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Diabetic macular edema (DME) remains a significant cause of vision loss despite the widespread use of anti-VEGF therapy. Nearly half of patients experience suboptimal responses in both anatomical and functional outcomes. This study correlates molecular signatures with clinical outcomes to identify associative markers of early treatment response and optimize DME management.

Methods

Serum samples from 44 DME patients, treated with ≥3 anti-VEGF injections and 6 months follow-up, classified as responders or non-responders. Multiplex bead-based assays were used to measure cytokines related to vascular integrity, inflammatory, and adhesion molecules. Statistical analysis was performed using GraphPad.

Results

Responders demonstrated improvement in BCVA from 20/63 (0.5 logMAR) to 20/35 (0.25 logMAR) and CRT (443 µm to 270 µm) (p < 0.01), while non-responders worsened in both parameters. The macular fluid area was 5-fold lower in responders (p < 0.001). Responders had higher Ang-1, sFLT-1, sST2, TNF-a, MCP-1( p< 0.01). Ang-1 and sFLT-1 correlated strongly with CRT reduction and improvement in BCVA. ROC analysis identified Ang-1, CRT (AUC = 0.9), and the Ang-1 ratio having superior diagnostic accuracy. Ang-1/sFLT-1 and Ang-1/sST2 ratios enhanced discrimination (AUC=0.9; p < 0.001).

Conclusion

Ang-1, sFLT-1, and sST2 are closely associated with treatment response to anti-VEGF therapy in DME patients, highlighting their roles in vascular integrity, endogenous VEGF blockade, and inflammation regulation. Both the cytokines individual levels and their ratios serve as early indicators of the success of anti-VEGF treatment in DME. Integrating these cytokines with BCVA and CRT measurements could enhance the efficiency of DME management.

records.title: PROGNOSTIC FACTORS FOR SECONDARY MACULAR HOLE DEVELOPMENT AFTER SURGERY FOR FOVEA-OFF RHEGMATOGENOUS RETINAL DETACHMENT AND POSTOPERATIVE VISUAL OUTCOMES.

content.title: PROGNOSTIC FACTORS FOR SECONDARY MACULAR HOLE DEVELOPMENT AFTER SURGERY FOR FOVEA-OFF RHEGMATOGENOUS RETINAL DETACHMENT AND POSTOPERATIVE VISUAL OUTCOMES.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate independent preoperative risk factors for secondary macular hole (MH) after fovea-off rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD) and their impact on postoperative visual outcomes.

Methods

This retrospective study included fovea-off RRD patients with preoperative optical coherence tomography (OCT) confirmed subfoveal fluid and complete pre- and postoperative demographics, clinical features, and OCT images. Based on postoperative OCT images, patients were subdivided into No MH, lamellar MH, and full-thickness MH groups after RRD surgery. Multivariate logistic regression and linear regression were applied to identify the factors associated with postoperative secondary MH and best-corrected visual acuity, respectively.

Results

Of these 705 patients, 57 developed secondary MH after RRD surgery, whereas the remaining 648 patients served as the control group. Multivariate logistic regression analysis demonstrated that Müller cell cone (MCC) loss (OR = 4.401, P = 0.001), bacillary layer detachment (OR = 2.528, P = 0.041), retinal detachment (RD) extent (OR = 1.136, P = 0.031), and foveal neurosensory thickness (OR = 0.992, P = 0.030) were independent MH risk factors. Multiple linear regression analysis showed that MCC loss (β = 0.308, P < 0.001), greater RD extent (β = 0.024, P = 0.010), longer RD duration (β = 0.001, P = 0.036), outer nuclear layer thinning (β = 0.144, P = 0.001), and worse preoperative best-corrected visual acuity (β = 0.129, P < 0.001) predicted poorer visual outcomes.

Conclusion

MCC loss is the strongest risk factor for both MH development and worse visual prognosis after RRD surgery.

records.title: Risk Factors for Retinal Pigment Epithelium Tears in Patients with Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Risk Factors for Retinal Pigment Epithelium Tears in Patients with Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Topic

To identify and synthesize clinical, imaging, and treatment-related risk factors associated with retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) tears in neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD).

Clinical relevance

RPE tears are a vision-threatening complication of nAMD, occurring most often in eyes with pigment epithelial detachments (PEDs) and frequently temporally associated with initiation of anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy. Improved recognition of high-risk PED features may enhance counseling and risk stratification.

Methods

This systematic review and meta-analysis followed PRISMA guidelines and was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251075278). MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched from inception to December 15, 2025. Randomized and non-randomized studies of adults (≥50 years) with nAMD evaluating candidate predictors of RPE tear were included. Two reviewers independently screened, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias (RoB 2, ROBINS-I). Random-effects meta-analyses were performed for baseline PED height and area, with per-study weighting, standardized mean difference (SMD), and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses. Certainty was assessed using GRADE.

Results

Sixteen studies comprising 4,043 eyes were included. Five studies (55 tear eyes; 370 controls; 425 eyes) showed greater baseline PED height in eyes developing tears (mean difference [MD], 212.39 µm; 95% confidence interval [CI], 133.87-290.91; I² = 24.6%; SMD, 1.09). Four studies (48 tear eyes; 1,312 controls; 1,360 eyes) showed larger baseline PED area (MD, 5.80 mm²; 95% CI, 3.48-8.12; I² = 2.7%; SMD, 0.88). Both persisted across all leave-one-out iterations; omitting the study contributing 43.5% of the area weight increased the effect (MD, 7.11 mm²). Fibrovascular PED, greater basal diameter and volume, subretinal fluid, sub-RPE clefts, radial hyperreflective lines, and occult or hemorrhagic macular neovascularization were also associated with tears. Anti-VEGF agent selection was not consistently associated. Most studies were at moderate to serious risk of bias; certainty was very low.

Conclusion

Baseline PED morphology, particularly increased height, is the most consistently reported association with RPE tear in nAMD. Because the evidence is predominantly retrospective, largely unadjusted, and of very low certainty, these are associations rather than validated predictive markers. Prospective studies using standardized imaging protocols are needed.

records.title: Comparative Analysis of Rhegmatogenous Retinal Detachment Repair with or without Associated Macular Hole.

content.title: Comparative Analysis of Rhegmatogenous Retinal Detachment Repair with or without Associated Macular Hole.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To assess the anatomic and functional outcomes in primary uncomplicated rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD) compared to RRD associated with macular hole (MH).

Methods

This retrospective cohort study included 1303 eyes with RRD and 30 eyes with MH-RRD operated on between 2014 and 2018 at a single tertiary center. Main outcomes were single-surgery anatomic success (SSAS), MH closure and final pinhole visual acuity (PHVA).

Results

Of the 1333 patients, 867 (65%) were male, and median [Q1, Q3] age was 63 [57, 70]. Most of these were macula-off detachments (n=764, 57%) with a higher proportion in MH-RRD (n=26, 87%) than primary RRD (n=738, 57%) (p=0.004). Baseline VA was lower in MH-RRD (p<0.001). Postoperative PHVA at three months was 0.30 [0.18, 0.54] in primary RRD vs. 0.85 [0.60, 1.30] in MH-RRD (p<0.001); final PHVA was 0.18 [0.10, 0.40] vs. 0.68 [0.40, 0.90] (p<0.001) respectively. Primary MH closure was achieved in 27 (90%) MH-RRD cases; at final follow-up, all 30 MH-RRDs had attached retinas with one persistent MH. MH presence was not significantly associated with SSAS (p=0.391), while increasing age was a negative predictor of SSAS (p=0.008). Male sex (p<0.001), SF6 tamponade (p<0.001), SSAS (p<0.001), and longer follow-up (p<0.001) were positive predictors of final PHVA.

Conclusion

SSAS did not significantly differ between the two groups though the small MH-RRD sample may have contributed to this. Functional outcomes were poorer in MH-RRD, likely due to more macula-off RRD, more retinal breaks, occasional MH closure failure and residual sequelae related to the MH.

records.title: Clinical assessment and relationship of retinal fluorophores and microvascular modifications in early diabetic retinal disease in type 1 diabetes.

content.title: Clinical assessment and relationship of retinal fluorophores and microvascular modifications in early diabetic retinal disease in type 1 diabetes.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To quantify macular microvascular modifications and retinal fluorophores in early diabetic retinal disease (DRD) in type 1 diabetes mellitus (DM1), and to explore their interrelationship.

Methods

One-hundred twenty-one subjects with DM1 and no diabetic retinopathy (noDR) or mild/moderate non-proliferative DR (NPDR) underwent optical coherence tomography (OCT), OCT-angiography (OCT-A), and spectrally resolved fundus autofluorescence (Sr-FAF). OCT-A was analyzed for perfusion/vessel density (PD/VD), fractal dimension (FD), vessel length density (VLD), geometric perfusion deficits (GPD), and foveal avascular zone metrics in the superficial and deep capillary plexuses (SCP/DCP). Sr-FAF green and red emission fluorescence component (GEFC/REFC) intensities in 9 ETDRS macular sectors were quantified. Mann-Whitney U test was used for group comparisons and Pearson's coefficients for correlations between OCT-A and Sr-FAF.

Results

One-hundred four eyes (50 noDR, 54 NPDR) were included. NPDR eyes showed lower PD, VD, FD, and VLD and higher GPD (p<0.001) in DCP vs noDR. GEFC intensity was higher in NPDR vs noDR in the nasal (p<0.01) and inner inferior (p=0.009) sectors and in the whole macular region(p=0.04); REFC intensity was higher in NPDR vs noDR at the fovea and in the inner nasal sector (p=0.01). In NPDR, DCP perfusion metrics correlated positively with GEFC and REFC values; in noDR, weak negative correlations were documented.

Conclusions

Quantification of minor retinal fluorophores with Sr-FAF and microvascular assessment may provide novel insights into early DRD in DM1. Opposing correlation trends across disease stages suggest dynamic vascular-metabolic interactions. Sr-FAF may serve as a biomarker of retinal metabolic status, warranting further validation.

records.title: Time Course of Resolution of Diabetic Macular Edema by Sustained Suppression of VEGF-A with the Port Delivery Platform with Ranibizumab.

content.title: Time Course of Resolution of Diabetic Macular Edema by Sustained Suppression of VEGF-A with the Port Delivery Platform with Ranibizumab.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To determine the incidence of poor responsiveness to VEGF-A suppression in eyes with diabetic macular edema (DME) by evaluating the effect of continuous delivery of ranibizumab via the Port Delivery Platform with ranibizumab (PDS) in individual patients enrolled in the Pagoda clinical trial.

Design

Retrospective analysis of prospective clinical trial data SUBJECTS: DME patients enrolled in Pagoda (NCT04108156).

Methods

Change in central subfield thickness (CST) and best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) over time was evaluated for the adjusted intent-to-treat (aITT) population in the Pagoda trial. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) images obtained at each visit were analyzed for 56 PDS subjects from 8 sites to determine the time course of changes in intraretinal and subretinal fluid.

Main outcome measures

CST, BCVA, and time to resolution of edema.

Results

In the aITT population the mean duration of follow up was 107.7 weeks in the PDS arm (n=272) and 100.7 weeks the IVT-PDS arm (n=238). The percentage of eyes with CST improvement into the normal range (≤325 µm) by the last visit was 87.9% in the PDS group and 85.3% in the IVT-PDS arm with mean time to normalization of 21.3 weeks and 20.6 weeks, respectively. All eyes in both arms showed reduction in CST over time although some exhibited periods of CST fluctuation and a few in each arm showed initial improvement followed by worsening at last follow up. In the eyes of 56 PDS patients that had detailed analysis of OCTs, normalization of CST occurred in 93% at a median of 17 weeks and elimination of intraretinal fluid in the central 1mm occurred in 84% at a median of 68 weeks. Only 3 of 56 eyes had poorly controlled DME at last follow up.

Conclusions

Sustained suppression of VEGF-A is sufficient to effectively treat DME in the vast majority of patients, but edema resolution may be slow in some patients giving the false impression of poor response to anti-VEGF-A treatment. In DME, the term unresponsive to anti-VEGF-A treatment should be replaced by slowly responsive.

records.title: Clinical outcomes of epiretinal membrane surgery in patients with good baseline visual acuity.

content.title: Clinical outcomes of epiretinal membrane surgery in patients with good baseline visual acuity.
content.abstract:
Purpose

For patients with symptomatic epiretinal membrane (ERM), pars plana vitrectomy (PPV) with ERM peel is often performed to improve their distortion. However, there is no clear consensus on visual acuity threshold for performing surgery, nor evidence of potential likelihood of risk to allow patients to make informed decisions.

Methods

A retrospective case notes review of visual outcomes and complications was performed at 4 UK surgical centres. All patients with symptomatic ERM and Snellen best corrected visual acuity (BCVA) of 20/40 or better (LogMAR 0.3 or better), were included. Outcome measures were BCVA at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months, as well as subjective improvement in symptoms, complications and further surgery.

Results

163 eyes of 163 patients were included in analysis. For this cohort, the mean pre-operative BCVA was equivalent to the mean post-operative BCVA. 80% (n=133) maintained or improved from their baseline VA of ≤20/40, whereas 1.2% (n=2) suffered major harm with post-operative BCVA of worse than 20/200. 92% of patients reported symptomatic improvement following surgery.

Conclusion

This study shows that for the vast majority of patients with symptomatic ERM but good visual acuity, pars plana vitrectomy and epiretinal membrane peel is a safe and successful surgery.

records.title: THE IMPACT OF RENAL FUNCTION ON PARS PLANA VITRECTOMY FOR PROLIFERATIVE DIABETIC RETINOPATHY AND ANALYSIS OF PROGNOSIS.

content.title: THE IMPACT OF RENAL FUNCTION ON PARS PLANA VITRECTOMY FOR PROLIFERATIVE DIABETIC RETINOPATHY AND ANALYSIS OF PROGNOSIS.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To observe and analyze the impact of renal function on pars plana vitrectomy for proliferative diabetic retinopathy.

Methods

This retrospective study included 110 patients (110 eyes) who were divided into an impaired renal function (IRF) group (52 eyes) and a normal renal function (NRF) group (58 eyes) based on chronic kidney disease staging. Patients were followed up and assessed preoperatively and throughout 1 year postoperatively. Independent risk factors affecting visual acuity recovery after pars plana vitrectomy were also identified.

Results

Compared with the NRF group, the IRF group had significantly longer diabetes duration, higher serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen, and lower hemoglobin and serum albumin (all P < 0.05). Preoperative laser treatment was more frequent in the NRF group, whereas intraoperative silicone oil tamponade was more common in the IRF group (both P < 0.05). Although the NRF group showed better best-corrected visual acuity at several postoperative time points ( P < 0.05), the final visual improvement rate at 12 months did not differ significantly between groups ( P = 0.156). No significant between-group differences were observed in postoperative complications. Multivariable analysis identified longer diabetes duration and lower serum albumin as independent risk factors for worse visual prognosis, whereas renal function itself was not an independent predictor.

Conclusion

Worse baseline best-corrected visual acuity, shorter diabetes duration, and higher serum albumin independently predicted postoperative visual improvement, whereas renal function itself did not. The poorer visual outcomes associated with renal impairment were likely attributable to greater ocular and systemic disease burden.

records.title: READING SPEED IN MACULAR TELANGIECTASIA TYPE 2: AN ANALYSIS OF SHAM PATIENTS IN THE REVAKINAGENE TARORETCEL-LWEY (NT-501) PHASE 3 TRIALS.

content.title: READING SPEED IN MACULAR TELANGIECTASIA TYPE 2: AN ANALYSIS OF SHAM PATIENTS IN THE REVAKINAGENE TARORETCEL-LWEY (NT-501) PHASE 3 TRIALS.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the relationship between best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) and reading speed in the sham-treated cohorts from two Phase 3 clinical trials of revakinagene taroretcel-lwey for macular telangiectasia type 2 (MacTel) and to determine whether reading speed captures functional decline not reflected by changes in BCVA.

Methods

This secondary analysis evaluated reading speed (words per minute [wpm] per eye using the International Reading Speed Test) and BCVA (Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Study letters) over 24 months. Associations between BCVA loss and reading speed decline were examined using multiple linear regression. Analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) assessed the effect of eye laterality on reading speed, controlling for baseline factors.

Results

Of 111 enrolled sham-treated eyes, 104 had complete data for analysis. For every 1-letter loss of BCVA, the reading speed decreased by 2.1 wpm (P < 0.0001). Sixty-eight eyes maintained stable BCVA (change of <5 letters) but experienced a statistically significant reading speed decline of 19.4 wpm over 24 months (P < 0.0001). An ANCOVA controlling for baseline factors revealed that left eyes were predicted to read approximately 18.5 wpm slower than right eyes at Month 24.

Conclusion

These findings suggest that BCVA may incompletely capture progressive functional vision loss in MacTel, whereas reading speed detected decline even when BCVA remained stable. Given its sensitivity and clinical relevance, reading speed may provide a meaningful endpoint for assessing MacTel progression and therapeutic efficacy and may also help clinicians quantify functional vision loss in routine practice.

records.title: EVALUATING THE EFFICACY AND SAFETY OF TOPICAL DIFLUPREDNATE IN PATIENTS WITH CHRONIC CENTRAL SEROUS CHORIORETINOPATHY.

content.title: EVALUATING THE EFFICACY AND SAFETY OF TOPICAL DIFLUPREDNATE IN PATIENTS WITH CHRONIC CENTRAL SEROUS CHORIORETINOPATHY.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the efficacy and safety of topical difluprednate ophthalmic emulsion 0.05% in chronic central serous chorioretinopathy (cCSCR) and compare its outcomes with oral eplerenone and observation.

Methods

This pilot open-label randomized controlled trial included patients with cCSCR of ≥3 months' duration or relapsing cases with subfoveal or juxtafoveal leakage on angiography. After baseline assessment, patients were randomized into three groups: topical difluprednate, oral eplerenone, or observation. All participants were followed monthly for 3 months. Changes in best-corrected visual acuity, optical coherence tomography parameters, retinal sensitivity, and adverse events were documented.

Results

A total of 53 adults (mean age 42.6 ± 9.5 years; 90.6% male) were enrolled. Complete resolution of subretinal fluid occurred in 90% (n = 18) of the patients in the difluprednate group, 45% (n = 9) in eplerenone group, and 23% (n = 3) patients in the control arm ( P < 0.001). The difluprednate group showed significantly greater reductions in subfoveal choroidal thickness and improvements in 3-mm microperimetry thresholds compared with the observation group ( P = 0.012 and P = 0.022, respectively). It also demonstrated the largest decrease in central macular thickness, although this was not statistically significant ( P = 0.19). Ocular hypertension developed in 30% of difluprednate-treated eyes and was controlled with topical antiglaucoma medication.

Conclusion

Topical difluprednate produced superior anatomical and functional improvements in subretinal fluid resolution, subfoveal choroidal thickness reduction, and retinal sensitivity within 3-mm when compared with oral eplerenone and observation. Thus, with a manageable safety profile, it may serve as an effective therapeutic option for cCSCR.

records.title: REAL-WORLD RETINAL VASCULITIS EVENTS REPORTED WITH FDA-APPROVED INTRAVITREAL ANTI-VEGF AND COMPLEMENT INHIBITOR AGENTS: An Analysis of FAERS Data.

content.title: REAL-WORLD RETINAL VASCULITIS EVENTS REPORTED WITH FDA-APPROVED INTRAVITREAL ANTI-VEGF AND COMPLEMENT INHIBITOR AGENTS: An Analysis of FAERS Data.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To analyze real-world Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) data for retinal vasculitis associated with approved intravitreal (IVT) anti-VEGF agents and complement inhibitors in the United States.

Methods

This retrospective study used the publicly available FAERS database to identify serious adverse events related to IVT anti-VEGF and complement inhibitor agents reported between January 2020 and December 2025. Reports for brolucizumab, faricimab, aflibercept, ranibizumab, pegcetacoplan, and avacincaptad pegol were analyzed, with data for aflibercept and ranibizumab also reviewed from 2010 to 2019. Events were filtered to include only those linked exclusively to a single agent. Retinal vasculitis adverse events (RVAEs) were identified using broad search terms related to vasculitis, while vascular occlusions without inflammation were excluded.

Results

FAERS data from January 2010 to December 2025 showed reported RVAEs across all included IVT therapies, with increased reporting after 2019. From January 2020 to December 2025, 554 RVAEs were identified among anti-VEGF reference products and complement inhibitors. Anti-VEGF reference products accounted for 485 reports (87.5%), and complement inhibitors accounted for 69 (12.5%). Brolucizumab accounted for the largest proportion (56.1%; 311/554), followed by faricimab (16.4%; 91/554), pegcetacoplan (11.9%; 66/554), aflibercept 2 mg (8.7%; 48/554), aflibercept 8 mg (4.2%; 23/554), ranibizumab (2.2%; 12/554), and avacincaptad pegol (0.5%; 3/554). Separate biosimilar analysis identified one aflibercept biosimilar RVAE and no ranibizumab biosimilar RVAEs during this updated study period overall.

Conclusions

FAERS reporting identified RVAEs across included IVT therapies, but cannot establish incidence, causality, or comparative risk, underscoring the need for vigilant reporting and ongoing post-marketing safety surveillance.

records.title: Prevalence of Diabetic Retinopathy and Cardiovascular Risk Factors Among Diverse Hispanic/Latino Adults: HCHS/SOL and SOL Ojos Results.

content.title: Prevalence of Diabetic Retinopathy and Cardiovascular Risk Factors Among Diverse Hispanic/Latino Adults: HCHS/SOL and SOL Ojos Results.
content.abstract:
Objective

To estimate diabetic retinopathy (DR) prevalence among Hispanic/Latino adults with diabetes, assess heterogeneity by background group, and evaluate cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk factors.

Design

Cross-sectional analysis of SOL Ojos, a multicenter ancillary study embedded within the population-based Hispanic Community Health Study/Study of Latinos (HCHS/SOL).

Participants

Adults aged ≥40 years completing HCHS/SOL Visit 3 (V3; 2020-2024) from Chicago and Miami were examined (3,294/3,864; 85.2%). The analytic sample included 1,224 participants with diabetes and gradable retinal imaging (mean age, 62.7 years [95% CI, 61.4-64.0]; 48.6% female).

Methods

Participants underwent standardized ophthalmic examinations with centrally graded ultra-widefield fundus imaging. Major CVD risk factors (diabetes, hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, obesity, smoking) were assessed at V3 and analyzed individually and cumulatively. DR, macular edema (ME), and vision-threatening DR (VTDR) were graded using Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Study (ETDRS) protocols. Survey-weighted analyses estimated age-standardized prevalence, and sequentially adjusted logistic regression evaluated associations.

Main outcome measures

Age-standardized prevalence of DR outcomes and associations with CVD risk factors.

Results

Age-standardized any DR prevalence was 34.7% (95% CI, 29.2-40.2). Among men, any DR and VTDR prevalence was 41.8% (95% CI, 33.5-50.0) and 13.4% (95% CI, 7.4-19.5), versus 27.2% (95% CI, 19.5-34.9) and 9.4% (95% CI, 1.4-17.4) among women. Any DR ranged across Hispanic/Latino backgrounds from 13.9% (95% CI, 1.8-26.0) to 55.4% (95% CI, 49.2-61.6) in men and 15.3% (95% CI, 4.4-26.2) to 39.2% (95% CI, 22.3-56.1) in women, with the highest estimates among Cuban individuals. CVD risk factors were common and clustered (≥4: men 42.7% [95% CI, 34.5-50.9]; women 35.6% [95% CI, 29.3-41.9]). In adjusted models, hypertension was associated with any DR (OR, 3.16 [95% CI, 1.76-5.65]) and VTDR (OR, 2.86 [95% CI, 1.05-7.79]). Overall cumulative CVD risk burden was not significantly associated with VTDR (Type III F test, P=0.1193), despite adjustment for diabetes duration; the 3-risk-factor category had higher estimated odds than the 1-risk-factor category (OR, 5.10 [95% CI, 1.22-21.39]).

Conclusion

In this cross-sectional study of Hispanic/Latino adults with diabetes, more than one-third had DR, with substantial heterogeneity across background groups. Hypertension was associated with DR outcomes, particularly VTDR. Findings provide contemporary prevalence estimates and support longitudinal evaluation of cardiometabolic risk and DR outcomes.

records.title: Regional and Temporal Changes in Choroidal Vascularity after Panretinal Photocoagulation in Diabetic Retinopathy: A Widefield SS-OCTA Study.

content.title: Regional and Temporal Changes in Choroidal Vascularity after Panretinal Photocoagulation in Diabetic Retinopathy: A Widefield SS-OCTA Study.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To investigate the changes in choroidal vasculature after panretinal photocoagulation (PRP) in patients with proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR) using widefield swept-source optical coherence tomography angiography (SS-OCTA).

Methods

Thirty eyes of 30 PDR patients were enrolled and underwent SS-OCTA examination before PRP, and at 1 month and 3 months after PRP. Twenty-two age-matched healthy volunteers served as controls. Choroidal thickness (ChT), choroidal vascular volume (CVV), choroidal vascularity index (CVI), choroidal stromal volume (CSV), choriocapillaris flow deficit percentage (CC FD%), and central macular thickness (CMT) were automatically measured within concentric rings of 2.5, 5, 12, and 19 mm centered on the fovea.

Results

Post-PRP choroidal changes showed distinct regional specificity and time dependence. In the periphery (12-19 mm): CVV decreased (-5.45% at 1 month, P=0.045; -8.23% at 3 months, P<0.001); CC FD% increased (+48.9% at 1 month, +80.7% at 3 months, both P<0.001); CVI decreased only at 3 months (-3.57%, P=0.011); CSV remained unchanged. In the central region (0-2.5 mm): except for a mild decrease in CVV at 3 months (-4.01%, P=0.009), all other parameters showed no significant changes. CMT progressively increased (+7.49 7.50% at 1 month, +12.32% at 3 months, both P<0.01). Exploratory analysis showed that centralΔCVV was independently positively correlated withΔCMT (β=0.219P=0.002) Exploratory regression analysis showed that baseline CMT and central ΔCVV were independently associated with ΔCMT (β=0.352, P=0.041; B=528.414, P=0.002, respectively).

Conclusion

PRP induces "vessel-first atrophy" in the periphery with relative central preservation, supporting hemodynamic redistribution. Widefield SS-OCTA effectively evaluates post-PRP choroidal changes. The association between central choroidal vascular volume change and macular edema requires further investigation.

records.title: EVALUATING CLINICAL OUTCOMES OF AMNIOTIC MEMBRANE COVERAGE COMBINED WITH EARLY VITRECTOMY IN THE MANAGEMENT OF PERFORATING GLOBE INJURIES.

content.title: EVALUATING CLINICAL OUTCOMES OF AMNIOTIC MEMBRANE COVERAGE COMBINED WITH EARLY VITRECTOMY IN THE MANAGEMENT OF PERFORATING GLOBE INJURIES.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the anatomical and functional outcomes of a surgical approach combining amniotic membrane coverage with early vitrectomy under low perfusion pressure in patients with perforating globe injuries.

Methods

The study involved 19 patients who presented with Zone 3 exit wounds of globe injuries. The surgical procedures included the administration of recombinant tissue plasminogen activator for hemorrhage clearance, pars plana vitrectomy, internal limiting membrane peeling or retinectomy depending on the presence of proliferative vitreoretinopathy, application of amniotic membrane over the exit wound, and intraocular tamponade injection. The postoperative follow-up period extended over 6 months.

Results

Anatomical success, defined as retinal reattachment, was achieved in 89.5% of cases, with a 100% rate of globe survival. The incidence of postoperative proliferative vitreoretinopathy was 10.5%. Best-corrected visual acuity improved in 89.47% of patients.

Conclusion

The combination of amniotic membrane coverage with early vitrectomy in the management of perforating globe injuries was associated with favorable anatomical outcomes, a low rate of postoperative proliferative vitreoretinopathy, and visual improvement in most patients. This approach represents a viable strategy for addressing the complex challenges in these severe ocular injuries.

records.title: SEVERE RETINAL NONPERFUSION IS ASSOCIATED WITH FEWER RETINAL LESIONS ON ULTRAWIDE-FIELD FUNDUS PHOTOGRAPHY IN PROLIFERATIVE DIABETIC RETINOPATHY.

content.title: SEVERE RETINAL NONPERFUSION IS ASSOCIATED WITH FEWER RETINAL LESIONS ON ULTRAWIDE-FIELD FUNDUS PHOTOGRAPHY IN PROLIFERATIVE DIABETIC RETINOPATHY.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To explore the relationship between the number of retinal lesions observed on ultrawide-field fundus photography (UWF-FP) and the nonperfusion index (NPI) quantified on UWF fluorescein angiography in patients with proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR).

Methods

The NPI was measured on early-phase UWF fluorescein angiography in 100 eyes from 100 patients with PDR, including both type 1 and type 2 diabetes. Eyes were divided into quartiles based on NPI values. Red dots (microaneurysms, retinal hemorrhages, and intraretinal microvascular abnormalities), venous beading, cotton-wool spots, and white thread-like arterioles were counted on UWF-FP.

Results

The mean NPI values for quartiles one to four were 2.8 ± 1.1%, 8.5 ± 2.1%, 17.3 ± 4.5%, and 42.8 ± 12.2%, respectively. Eyes in the highest NPI quartile (quartile 4) had significantly fewer retinal lesions on UWF-FP (76.1 ± 50.6) and fewer cotton-wool spots compared with those in the lowest NPI quartile, which showed 253.0 ± 165.5 retinal lesions ( P < 0.001). White thread-like arterioles were present in 80.0% of eyes in quartile four and none in quartile 1. Patients in quartile four were predominantly type 2 diabetics with higher rates of end-stage kidney disease, peripheral neuropathy, lower-extremity peripheral artery disease, and prior limb amputation or revascularization.

Conclusion

In patients with poorly controlled, long-standing type 2 diabetes complicated by renal failure, peripheral neuropathy, peripheral arterial disease, or lower-limb amputation, fluorescein angiography should be considered when highly ischemic PDR is suspected, particularly in the presence of white thread-like arterioles, as it may otherwise appear milder on color fundus photography.

records.title: PROGNOSTIC FACTORS FOR CLINICAL OUTCOMES AND LESION REACTIVATION IN STAGE 2 to 3 TYPE 3 MACULAR NEOVASCULARIZATION TREATED USING a TREAT-AND-EXTEND REGIMEN.

content.title: PROGNOSTIC FACTORS FOR CLINICAL OUTCOMES AND LESION REACTIVATION IN STAGE 2 to 3 TYPE 3 MACULAR NEOVASCULARIZATION TREATED USING a TREAT-AND-EXTEND REGIMEN.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the treatment outcomes of Type 3 macular neovascularization and identify factors associated with visual outcomes and lesion reactivation during 76 weeks of aflibercept therapy using a treat-and-extend (TAE) regimen.

Methods

This post hoc analysis included 25 treatment-naive patients with Stage 2 to 3 Type 3 macular neovascularization who participated in a previous prospective study and received aflibercept treatment for 76 weeks using a TAE regimen. The incidence and outcomes of the first lesion reactivation were assessed. Factors associated with lesion reactivation and best-corrected visual acuity at the final visit were evaluated.

Results

Lesion reactivation occurred in 8 patients (32.0%) during the treatment period; however, no patient experienced a loss of ≥5 letters before or after the first reactivation. In multivariate analysis, best-corrected visual acuity at Week 16 was a strong predictor of final best-corrected visual acuity ( P < 0.001, β = 1.191), and older age was significantly associated with a lower risk of lesion reactivation ( P = 0.036, β = 0.811).

Conclusion

Early visual outcomes after the initial loading injections can serve as reliable prognostic indicators for long-term treatment of Stage 2 to 3 Type 3 macular neovascularization using a TAE regimen. In younger patients, the increased likelihood of lesion reactivation should be considered. Although lesion reactivation occurred in approximately one third of the patients, it did not result in significant visual deterioration. Further studies analyzing treatment outcomes in Stage 1 disease are required.

records.title: Macular holes and endogenous electric fields A Theoretical Model Of How Electrotaxis In Retinal Glial Cells Aids In Macular Hole Closure.

content.title: Macular holes and endogenous electric fields A Theoretical Model Of How Electrotaxis In Retinal Glial Cells Aids In Macular Hole Closure.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To introduce the concept of endogenous electric fields in macular hole closure and propose them as a plausible mechanism guiding retinal glial cell migration to facilitate closure.

Methods

This theoretical model reviews the current literature on electrotaxis as a well-established mechanism of cell migration in wound healing, particularly in tissues such as cornea and skin. These principles are then applied to the unique bioelectric environment of the retina, with analysis focused on Müller cells and the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) as critical ion regulators capable of generating endogenous fields.

Results

The model proposes that ionic fluxes across the RPE and Müller cells can generate EEFs sufficient to direct electrotaxis, thereby providing a plausible biological explanation for the success of diverse surgical techniques. From ILM peeling to autologous or heterologous tissue transplantation, these interventions may restore or enhance the bioelectric environment necessary for glial-mediated closure.

Conclusion

Endogenous electric fields may represent a previously unrecognized but potentially central mechanism in macular hole resolution. This unifying theory illuminates the cellular drivers underlying successful closure, explains existing surgical outcomes, and may inform novel, biology-driven therapeutic strategies to improve patient care.

records.title: ULTRAWIDE-FIELD COLOR FUNDUS IMAGES AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR DIAGNOSIS OF DIABETIC RETINOPATHY: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: ULTRAWIDE-FIELD COLOR FUNDUS IMAGES AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR DIAGNOSIS OF DIABETIC RETINOPATHY: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Ultrawide-field (UWF) fundus cameras capture a larger retinal area without pupil dilation. The authors summarized evidence and diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven diabetic retinopathy (DR) assessments using UWF images (UWFIs).

Methods

The authors searched PubMed, Scopus, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science to February 9, 2025, for studies evaluating DR using UWFIs and AI analyses. They followed the PRISMA guidelines and assessed study quality using the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist for diagnostic accuracy. Forest plots and summary receiver operating characteristic curves estimated sensitivity and specificity of AI-driven DR screening using UWFI.

Results

Of 527 records identified, 17 studies were included in the systematic review and four in the meta-analysis. All studies used Optos software. Among the included studies, two evaluated DR discrimination from multiple retinal disorders, six addressed DR stage classification based on guideline scales, six evaluated DR screening, and one each focused on referable retinal pathology detection, DR progression prediction, and detection of clinical DR features. The summary sensitivity, specificity, and area under receiver operating characteristic curve for AI-driven DR screening using UWFI were 85.0%, 72.5%, and 0.870 (0.838-0.897), respectively. UWFI-based AI screening showed acceptable sensitivity but limited specificity.

Conclusion

AI-driven DR screening using UWFIs may achieve acceptable sensitivity but with limited specificity; however, these findings should be interpreted with caution, given the limited number of available studies. Further studies using larger, diverse data sets with rigorous external validation across UWF platforms are needed to improve generalizability and clarify the clinical role of UWFI-based AI.

records.title: THE IMPACT OF THE ECTOPIC INNER FOVEAL LAYER WITH PRESERVED FOVEAL CONTOUR ON RETINAL MICROVASCULATURE CHANGES AFTER EPIRETINAL MEMBRANE REMOVAL.

content.title: THE IMPACT OF THE ECTOPIC INNER FOVEAL LAYER WITH PRESERVED FOVEAL CONTOUR ON RETINAL MICROVASCULATURE CHANGES AFTER EPIRETINAL MEMBRANE REMOVAL.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the long-term effects of preoperative ectopic inner foveal layer (EIFL) with preserved foveal contour on postoperative retinal microvascular changes in patients with epiretinal membrane.

Methods

Patients were divided into two groups based on EIFL presence: Group 1 without EIFL and Group 2 with EIFL. Superficial and deep vessel densities (SVDs and DVDs), corresponding to the superficial and deep vascular complexes, were quantitatively assessed using OCT angiography.

Results

The SVDs at baseline, 1, 3, 6, and 12 months were 27.9 ± 7.7, 27.6 ± 8.3, 25.9 ± 7.8, 26.1 ± 7.0, and 24.9 ± 8.0% in Group 1, respectively ( P = 0.075), and 31.6 ± 7.3, 28.0 ± 6.3, 26.7 ± 5.6, 25.4 ± 5.7, and 22.9 ± 5.6% in Group 2, respectively ( P < 0.001). The DVDs were 21.9 ± 4.6, 22.9 ± 4.5, 23.6 ± 5.1, 24.2 ± 4.0, and 23.6 ± 4.7% in Group 1, respectively ( P = 0.277), and 20.6 ± 4.7, 22.8 ± 4.2, 23.2 ± 3.7, 23.6 ± 5.0, and 23.4 ± 3.8% in Group 2, respectively ( P = 0.003). In the multivariable analysis, baseline BCVA was significantly associated with changes in BCVA in Group 1, whereas in Group 2, baseline BCVA and DVD showed significant associations with BCVA changes.

Conclusion

Patients with EIFL and preserved foveal contour demonstrated more prominent alterations in retinal microvasculature after surgery, and these changes, especially within the deep vascular complex, are considered to play an important role in visual improvement.

records.title: Retinal phenotypes and longitudinal clinical courses in patients with NPHP1-associated Senior-Løken syndrome.

content.title: Retinal phenotypes and longitudinal clinical courses in patients with NPHP1-associated Senior-Løken syndrome.
content.abstract:
Purpose

This study aimed to describe retinal phenotype, longitudinal clinical course, and genetic findings in Japanese patients with NPHP1-associated Senior-Løken syndrome and their siblings.

Design

Retrospective, multicenter case series.

Patients and methods

This study included 12 patients with biallelic pathogenic NPHP1 variants, comprising 10 probands with symptomatic retinal dystrophy recruited from six ophthalmic centers across Japan and 2 affected siblings identified through family screening. Clinical and genetic findings were analyzed. Retinal dystrophy was diagnosed using fundus photography, fundus autofluorescence (FAF), optical coherence tomography, and electroretinography. Genetic testing was performed using whole-exome and/or whole-genome sequencing. Follow-up ranged from 0 to 44 years (mean, 14.6 years).

Main outcome measures

Retinal phenotype, onset of retinopathy and nephropathy, and genotype.

Results

Retinal phenotypes included cone/cone-rod dystrophy (4 patients), retinitis pigmentosa (4 patients), sector retinitis pigmentosa (2 patients), pigmented paravenous retinochoroidal atrophy (1 patient), and normal retina (1 patient). FAF images showed a descending tract in 5 patients. Retinopathy preceded nephropathy in 9 patients, all of whom were initially diagnosed with Leber congenital amaurosis or early-onset retinal dystrophy. Genetic testing showed that 11 patients harbored a homozygous whole-NPHP1 deletion, whereas 1 carried compound heterozygous NPHP1 and EYS variants.

Conclusions

Patients with NPHP1-associated Senior-Løken syndrome showed considerable inter- and intrafamilial variability in retinal phenotype. Pigmented paravenous retinochoroidal atrophy can be associated with NPHP1 variants. A descending tract on FAF imaging may be a characteristic feature of retinal degeneration in Senior-Løken syndrome. Retinopathy, which commonly manifests as Leber congenital amaurosis or early-onset retinal dystrophy, often precedes nephropathy in patients with NPHP1-associated Senior-Løken syndrome.

records.title: Lichen Simplex Chronicus is Associated with an Increased Risk of Rhegmatogenous Retinal Detachment and Retinal Tears: A Propensity Score-Matched Cohort Study.

content.title: Lichen Simplex Chronicus is Associated with an Increased Risk of Rhegmatogenous Retinal Detachment and Retinal Tears: A Propensity Score-Matched Cohort Study.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To determine whether lichen simplex chronicus (LSC) is associated with an increased risk of rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD) and retinal tears without detachment (RT) compared with adults without LSC.

Methods

This retrospective propensity score-matched cohort study used TriNetX to compare adults (≥18 years) with LSC to matched adults without LSC. Patients with prior RRD, RT, ocular trauma, or proliferative diabetic retinopathy were excluded. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed on demographics, ocular and systemic comorbidities, and prior ophthalmology encounters. Incidence of RRD, RT, the composite endpoint of RRD or RT (RRD/RT), retinopexy, RRD repair, and the composite of RRD repair or retinopexy were compared using risk analysis and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis with Cox regression, yielding risk ratios (RR) and hazard ratios (HR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI).

Results

After 1:1 propensity score matching, the study included 64,170 patients per group. LSC patients had significantly higher rates of RRD (RR 8.83, 95% CI 4.86-16.05; p<0.001), RT (RR 10.15, 95% CI 6.79-15.19; p<0.001), and composite RRD/RT (RR 9.60, 95% CI 6.78-13.60; p<0.001). On procedure analysis, retinopexy (RR 6.64, 95% CI 3.52-12.51; p<0.001), RRD repair (RR 4.07, 95% CI 2.27-7.31; p<0.001), and the composite of retinopexy or RRD repair (RR 5.08, 95% CI 3.28-7.87; p<0.001) occurred more frequently in the LSC cohort.

Conclusion

LSC is associated with a substantially increased risk of incident diagnosis of RRD, RT, composite RRD/RT, and their procedural repair after adjustment for known risk factors. These findings suggest LSC may increase the risk of rhegmatogenous retinal pathology.

records.title: EFFICACY AND SAFETY OF SUBTHRESHOLD LASER IN PATIENTS WITH ACUTE CENTRAL SEROUS CHORIORETINOPATHY: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

content.title: EFFICACY AND SAFETY OF SUBTHRESHOLD LASER IN PATIENTS WITH ACUTE CENTRAL SEROUS CHORIORETINOPATHY: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Subthreshold laser has been proposed as a potentially safer and more effective alternative for patients with acute central serous chorioretinopathy (CSC). Hence, the objective of this systematic review was to assess the efficacy and safety of subthreshold laser treatment for acute CSC.

Methods

We performed a comprehensive systematic search of PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, and CENTRAL from their inception up to March 24, 2026. We included randomized controlled trials comparing the efficacy and/or safety of subthreshold laser against any comparator. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted, and the certainty of evidence was rated using the minimally contextualized GRADE approach.

Results

Six randomized controlled trials (401 participants) in patients with acute CSC were included. Compared with conventional laser, subthreshold laser probably yields similar improvements in visual acuity and reduces retinal pigment epithelium damage but probably leads to a lower rate of subretinal fluid resolution. When compared with observation, subthreshold laser may result in similar visual acuity outcomes but may reduce persistent metamorphopsia and increase subretinal fluid resolution, although the certainty of evidence is very low. Compared with half-dose photodynamic therapy, subthreshold laser may provide comparable visual outcomes but lower anatomical improvement, with very low certainty of evidence.

Conclusion

In acute CSC, subthreshold laser appears safer than conventional laser and produces similar visual outcomes, although its anatomical efficacy is limited. Its potential advantages over observation or photodynamic therapy remain uncertain because of low-certainty evidence.

records.title: 3D Corneal and Retinal Bioprinting: Tissue Engineering Strategies, Translational Challenges, and Clinical Opportunities.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: 3D Corneal and Retinal Bioprinting: Tissue Engineering Strategies, Translational Challenges, and Clinical Opportunities.
content.abstract: Three-dimensional bioprinting has emerged as a promising strategy for addressing major unmet needs in ophthalmology, including the global shortage of donor corneal tissue and the absence of restorative therapies for retinal degenerative disease. Advances in biomaterials, stem cell biology, and biofabrication have enabled increasingly sophisticated ocular constructs, ranging from engineered corneal grafts to multicellular retinal models that recapitulate key aspects of native tissue architecture. However, substantial challenges remain in reproducing the optical, mechanical, and biological functions required for clinical translation. This review critically evaluates the current state of corneal and retinal bioprinting through a framework organized around tissue target, fabrication modality, and intended application. Major bioprinting approaches, including extrusion-based, laser-assisted, drop-on-demand, and light-based technologies, are compared with respect to resolution, cell compatibility, scalability, and translational potential. Particular emphasis is placed on the engineering constraints governing construct fidelity, bioink design, tissue integration, and long-term functional performance. Current evidence suggests that corneal and retinal bioprinting have progressed along distinct translational trajectories. Corneal bioprinting has achieved encouraging preclinical outcomes, with selected approaches entering early clinical evaluation, whereas retinal bioprinting has generated highly informative disease models but remains at an earlier stage of translational development. Across both tissues, the field has increasingly shifted from reproducing individual cellular components toward reconstructing the biological interfaces and multicellular systems that underlie tissue function. Future progress will depend on establishing functional validation frameworks, reproducible manufacturing workflows, and standardized benchmarks to support the clinical development of vision-restoring bioprinted constructs.

records.title: Seeing in tandem: Cis and trans-regulation of tandemly-duplicated cone opsin genes in zebrafish.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Seeing in tandem: Cis and trans-regulation of tandemly-duplicated cone opsin genes in zebrafish.
content.abstract: The molecular basis for vertebrate color vision is expression of spectrally-selective opsin-based photopigments within distinct cone photoreceptor populations. In several primates including humans, and in numerous fish species, genes encoding duplicated, spectrally-divergent cone opsin proteins may be positioned in tandem arrays. This article reviews studies of the regulation of differential expression of these duplicated cone opsin genes in humans and fish, with an emphasis on knowledge derived from the zebrafish model. In humans, the long wavelength-sensitive/medium wavelength-sensitive (LWS/MWS; red/green) tandemly-duplicated array underlies trichromatic color vision; mutations in this array cause altered color vision and retinal degenerations. A foundational model posited that regulation of human LWS vs. MWS opsin expression is stochastic, whereby an upstream enhancer associates randomly with promoters of the proximal or distal gene, and one of these associations becomes permanent. Discoveries of tandemly-duplicated cone opsin genes in teleost fish, including the versatile zebrafish model, led to their use to further pursue mechanisms of differential expression. The tandemly-duplicated zebrafish lws1 and lws2 genes (encoding red-sensing cone opsins) share a common ancestral gene with human LWS and MWS. Subsequent studies revealed that differential expression of these genes is regulated by the paracrine signal retinoic acid (RA) and the endocrine signal thyroid hormone (TH). Further investigations identified additional cone transcripts distinguishing zebrafish LWS1 vs. LWS2 cones, plasticity of cone opsin expression across the lifespan in response to TH, and a candidate receptor and cis-regulatory element. The findings warrant updates to the foundational model and further consideration of hypotheses for regulation of the human LWS vs. MWS genes.

records.title: Ocular Changes in Human Spaceflight.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Ocular Changes in Human Spaceflight.
content.abstract: Spaceflight presents unique challenges to ocular health, with astronauts experiencing a range of visual disturbances in the setting of microgravity, radiation exposure, and other environmental factors. This review synthesizes knowledge about how spaceflight affects ocular anatomy and function. We outline the diagnostic and therapeutic limitations in microgravity, including constraints on imaging modalities, intracranial pressure measurement, and drug delivery. In addition, we examine common spaceflight-associated ocular pathologies, including spaceflight-associated neuro-ocular syndrome, corneal epithelial disruption, possible radiation-associated lens changes, and retinal or choroidal alterations. Drawing from evidence across human missions, terrestrial analogs, and experimental models, this review emphasizes the critical importance of vision to astronaut safety and mission success. Future directions include long-term ocular health monitoring, advancement of in-flight diagnostic capabilities, and multidisciplinary strategies to safeguard astronaut vision.

records.title: AI-ASSISTED OCT BIOMARKER QUANTIFICATION REVEALS DISTINCT RETINAL FLUID TRAJECTORIES IN CENTRAL RETINAL VEIN OCCLUSION.

content.title: AI-ASSISTED OCT BIOMARKER QUANTIFICATION REVEALS DISTINCT RETINAL FLUID TRAJECTORIES IN CENTRAL RETINAL VEIN OCCLUSION.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To characterize longitudinal patterns of intraretinal (IRF) and subretinal fluid (SRF) dynamics using artificial intelligence-assisted optical coherence tomography (OCT) biomarker quantification and to evaluate their association with long-term visual outcomes in eyes with central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO).

Methods

Patients with previously treatment-naïve CRVO and a documented 24-month follow-up were retrospectively included. All eyes received intravitreal aflibercept administered according to a treat-and-extend protocol. Spectral-domain OCT scans were analyzed at baseline and after 3 and 24 months. IRF and SRF volumes were quantified using RetinAI Discovery OCT Biomarker Detector (Ikerian AG). Linear regression models were used to assess the association between fluid volumes and 24-month corrected distance visual acuity (CDVA). Patients were clustered according to their IRF trajectories over time to identify distinct fluid-response phenotypes.

Results

Out of 173 patients, 64 eyes (64 patients) were included. Baseline IRF and SRF volumes showed no significant association with 24-month CDVA. Cluster analysis of longitudinal IRF trajectories identified four distinct fluid-response patterns. Eyes with low or rapidly resolving IRF achieved the best long-term visual outcomes (median CDVA 73 letters), whereas those with persistent or recurrent IRF showed poorer outcomes (median 53 letters; P = 0.008). Early IRF resolution tended to predict superior visual recovery at 24 months.

Conclusion

Artificial intelligence-based volumetric OCT analysis suggests that distinct retinal fluid trajectories in CRVO may have prognostic implications for long-term visual acuity, although these findings are preliminary and require validation. Dynamic IRF resolution patterns may be more informative than static fluid volumes for predicting functional outcomes after anti-vascular endothelial growth factor therapy.

records.title: Association of Retinal Microvascular Density with Hemodynamic and Clinical Severity Markers in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.

content.title: Association of Retinal Microvascular Density with Hemodynamic and Clinical Severity Markers in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate whether quantitative retinal microvascular and structural parameters, measured by optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA), are associated with disease severity and right ventriculo-arterial coupling in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH).

Methods

This cross-sectional study included 45 patients with confirmed PAH, stratified by New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class (I-III). Patients with coexisting ocular pathologies were strictly excluded. Vessel density (VD) in the superficial (SCP) and deep capillary plexuses (DCP), foveal avascular zone characteristics, and ganglion cell complex (GCC) thickness were analyzed. These parameters were correlated with functional capacity (6-minute walk test [6-mWT]), NT-proBNP levels, and the echocardiographic TAPSE/sPAP ratio.

Results

Retinal VD in both SCP and DCP progressively decreased with worsening NYHA functional class (p < 0.05). Retinal VD showed a significant negative correlation with NT-proBNP levels (r = -0.355, p = 0.017) and a positive correlation with 6-mWT distance (r = 0.499, p < 0.001). Crucially, retinal microvascular density demonstrated a robust positive correlation with the TAPSE/sPAP ratio (r = 0.420, p = 0.004), a surrogate for right ventriculo-arterial coupling. GCC thickness exhibited variations across NYHA classes but lacked a consistent linear progression.

Conclusion

Retinal microvascular attenuation in PAH is strongly associated not only with functional and biochemical severity but also with central hemodynamic impairment represented by the TAPSE/sPAP ratio. These findings suggest that OCTA-derived vessel density may serve as a promising, non-invasive biomarker for monitoring systemic microvascular compromise and right heart function in PAH.

records.title: Retina Insurance Reimbursements of Pediatric Retina Patients in a Hospital versus Outpatient Surgical Setting.

content.title: Retina Insurance Reimbursements of Pediatric Retina Patients in a Hospital versus Outpatient Surgical Setting.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate reimbursement patterns for pediatric vitreoretinal procedures performed at a tertiary children's hospital versus an ambulatory surgery center (ASC).

Methods

A retrospective review was conducted of retinal procedures in pediatric patients performed between 1/2022 and 1/2025 at a tertiary children's hospital and an ambulatory surgery center in Texas. Self-pay visits and visits with zero billed charges were excluded. The primary outcome was total median reimbursement percentage based on physician-level services. Secondary outcomes included median reimbursement percentage by payer type, public insurer subgroup, surgical setting, and current procedural terminology (CPT) code. The proportion of visits with zero reimbursement was also evaluated.

Results

394 visits from 282 patients were analyzed, including 219 visits at the children's hospital and 175 at the ASC. Median reimbursement was 34.0% (representing 85% of the equivalent Medicare reimbursement rate). Public insurers reimbursed a higher median percentage than private insurers (35.1% vs. 26.5%, P=0.001). Reimbursement was lower at the hospital than the ASC (29.1% vs 36.3%, P<0.0001). 24.1% of visits received zero payment, occurring more frequently among privately insured than publicly insured visits (30.8% vs. 17.3%, P=0.003). Complex retinal detachment repair reimbursed less for private than public insurers (35.4% vs. 42.7%, P< 0.001).

Conclusion

Private insurers reimbursed lower than public insurers for pediatric vitreoretinal procedures, contrary to patterns commonly reported in adult retinal care. Procedures performed at a tertiary children's hospital resulted in lower reimbursements than those performed at an ASC. Frequent zero-payment encounters, particularly among private insurers, pose challenges that adversely affect the financial sustainability of pediatric retinal care.

records.title: Persistent opioid use in cataract surgery pain management and the role of nonopioid alternatives.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Persistent opioid use in cataract surgery pain management and the role of nonopioid alternatives.
content.abstract: Cataracts are a leading cause of preventable blindness globally. Although care varies between developing and industrialized countries, surgery is the single effective approach to treating cataracts. From the earliest documented primitive cataract removals to today's advanced techniques, cataract surgery has evolved dramatically. As surgical techniques have developed, so have approaches to surgical pain management. With current cataract surgical procedures and advanced technology, anesthesia and intraoperative pain management have shifted to topical/intracameral anesthetics, with or without low-dose systemic analgesia and anxiolysis. Despite this, pain and discomfort persist in some patients and are underappreciated in modern cataract surgery. Although pain management has progressed, opioids remain a mainstay intraoperatively and, to a lesser extent, postoperatively. This article discusses the evolution of pain management in cataract surgery, particularly the use of opioids and the associated risks as well as how ophthalmology can have a positive impact on the opioid crisis.

records.title: Influence of capsular tension ring implantation on dynamic in vivo capsular apposition and intraocular lens behavior in highly myopic eyes.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Influence of capsular tension ring implantation on dynamic in vivo capsular apposition and intraocular lens behavior in highly myopic eyes.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the dynamic in vivo capsular apposition to the intraocular lens (IOL) in highly myopic eyes after capsular tension ring (CTR) implantation using swept-source optical coherence tomography (SS-OCT), and to investigate its correlation with in-the-bag IOL behavior.

Setting

Eye Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University, Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province, China.

Design

Prospective randomized clinical trial.

Methods

Highly myopic patients undergoing cataract surgery were randomized to receive CTR implantation or not. SS-OCT was performed at 1 day, 1 week, 1 month, 3 months, and 6 months to assess capsular apposition. Postoperative aqueous depth (PAD), IOL rotation, and anterior and posterior capsular opacification (ACO/PCO) were evaluated at each follow-up visit.

Results

A total of 29 eyes with CTR implantation and 30 eyes without CTR were included. The CTR group exhibited accelerated anterior capsular apposition, demonstrated by a smaller lens-anterior capsule distance (LCD) at 1 day and a higher proportion of anterior capsular apposition at 1 week. From 1 month onward, posterior capsular apposition occurred more frequently in the CTR group. At 1 day, the average LCD positively correlated with both PAD and IOL rotation. During subsequent follow-up period, the mean capsular bend index exhibited negative correlations with the absolute changes in PAD and IOL rotational speed. The CTR group developed less severe ACO, eyes with incomplete posterior capsular apposition had a higher risk of PCO.

Conclusions

CTR implantation facilitates accelerated anterior and more complete posterior capsular apposition to the IOL in highly myopic eyes, which may contribute to improved postoperative IOL stability and a reduced incidence of capsular opacification.

records.title: Comparison of the Moussa Intraocular Lens Formula to contemporary formulas in a multicenter study.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Comparison of the Moussa Intraocular Lens Formula to contemporary formulas in a multicenter study.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the refractive predictive accuracy of the Moussa intraocular lens (IOL) formula compared with Kane, EVO, PEARL-DGS, K6, Hoffer-QST, and Barrett Universal II (BUII).

Setting

Birmingham Midland Eye Centre (Birmingham), Manchester Royal Eye Hospital and Newmedica (Manchester), UK.

Design

Multicenter, retrospective, consecutive, nonrandomized observational case series (September 2022-June 2025).

Methods

Included were one eye per patient undergoing uncomplicated phacoemulsification. Preoperative biometry used the IOLMaster 700, Lenstar LS900, or Pentacam AXL Wave. Lens-constants were optimized to zero mean prediction error (PE) for each formula and lens-biometer combination. Primary outcome was mean absolute error (MAE), evaluated using heteroscedastic studentized bootstrap analysis (2000 iterations; Holm correction). Secondary outcomes included median absolute error, root-mean-square error, standard deviation of PE, and proportions of eyes within ±0.25diopter (D) and ±0.50D.

Results

Included were 2550 patients (2550 eyes; mean age 74.0±10.0 years; 1068 male patients [41.9%]). Moussa produced a lower MAE (0.348 D) than Kane (0.359D), EVO (0.363D), PEARL-DGS (0.367D), K6 (0.367D), Hoffer-QST (0.377D), and BUII (0.379D; all p<.001). In short eyes (≤22.0mm), Moussa (0.412D) demonstrated lower error than K6 (p<.001), BUII (p<.001), Hoffer-QST (p=.008), EVO (p=.008), PEARL-DGS (p=.014), and Kane (p=.039). In long eyes (≥26.0 mm), Moussa (0.342 D) had lower error than Kane, BUII, Hoffer-QST (all p<.001), and K6 (p=.045), but not EVO (p=.068) or PEARL-DGS (p=.202).

Conclusions

The Moussa formula demonstrated high predictive accuracy across multiple biometry platforms, with statistically lower overall MAE than the comparator formulas. Absolute differences from the closest-performing formulas were modest, and ±0.50D outcomes were similar to Kane and EVO. These findings support Moussa as a clinically relevant contemporary option for IOL power calculation, with encouraging results in short and long eyes requiring further targeted validation.

records.title: Improving effective lens position prediction for secondary intraocular lens implantation in pediatric aphakic eyes.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Improving effective lens position prediction for secondary intraocular lens implantation in pediatric aphakic eyes.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To improve the accuracy of refractive prediction for pediatric secondary sulcus intraocular lens (IOL) implantation by optimizing the effective lens position (ELP) prediction within the SRK/T formula.

Setting

Zhongshan Ophthalmic Center, Guangzhou, China.

Design
