content.title: Small Incision Lenticule Extraction (SMILE) Versus Laser Assisted Stromal In Situ Keratomileusis (LASIK) for Astigmatism Corrections: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare small incision lenticule extraction (SMILE) and laser assisted stromal in situ keratomileusis (LASIK) for astigmatism correction.

Design

Systematic review and meta-analysis METHODS: We reviewed published studies comparing outcomes after LASIK and SMILE for astigmatism correction by querying PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane, and Web of Science, with a cut-off date of September 3, 2022. We also compared the changes in visual acuity, refraction, and high-order aberrations between the surgeries. Astigmatism correction outcomes in the low-to-moderate group (less than or equal to -2.00 D) and high group (greater than -2.00 D) were evaluated using vector analysis. The Cochrane risk of bias tool in RevMan software was used for randomized studies (RCT), and Risk Of Bias In Nonrandomized Studies - of Interventions (ROBINS-I) was used for the nonrandomized studies (NRSs).

Results

There were 17 studies (5 randomized studies and 12 cohort studies), including 1,985 eyes. A statistically significant difference was found in the correction index (mean difference [MD] = -0.02, 95% confidence interval [CI] = -0.04 to -0.01, P =0.01), although there was no significant difference in the index of success (MD = 0.01, 95% CI = -0.03 to 0.05, P =0.51), different vector (MD = 0.07, 95% CI = 0.00 to 0.13, P =0.04), and angle of error (MD = 0.56, 95% CI = -0.34 to 1.45, P =0.22) between SMILE and LASIK. However, for low-to-moderate astigmatism correction, SMILE exhibited a smaller correction index (MD = -0.08, 95% CI= -0.13 to -0.02, P =0.008) and a larger difference vector (MD = 0.18, 95% CI = 0.09 to 0.27, P <0.0001) than LASIK. There was no significant difference between the different procedures in visual acuity and refraction (spherical equivalent: MD = -0.04, 95% CI = -0.08 to 0.01, P =0.15) or high-order aberration (MD = -0.01, 95% CI = -0.07 to 0.04, P =0.67), except spherical aberration (MD = -0.12, 95% CI = -0.23 to -0.01, P =0.04). The risk of bias was moderate in most studies because of poor reporting of several bias domains for RCTs, and because of confounding and selective outcome reporting for NRSs.

Conclusions

When used to treat severe astigmatism, both SMILE and LASIK provide effective and predictable results and generally have equivalent outcomes. However, evidence reveals a tendency toward undercorrection in the SMILE groups for astigmatism correction. In addition, LASIK has a greater probability of causing postoperative spherical aberration.

records.title: Changing Patterns of Dry Eye Disease Management in Korea: A Nationwide 10-Year Analysis.

content.title: Changing Patterns of Dry Eye Disease Management in Korea: A Nationwide 10-Year Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To investigate long-term trends in treated dry eye disease (DED) prevalence and medication prescribing patterns in Korea using a nationwide mandatory insurance claims database.

Design

Retrospective nationwide clinical cohort study.

Participants

Patients identified from the Korean NHIS mandatory claims database (2014-2023).

Methods

DED was defined by at least one relevant ICD-10 diagnosis code together with at least one prescription for a DED-related topical medication within the same calendar year. Annual overall, sex-specific, and age-specific prevalence was calculated using the corresponding mid-year resident population. Medication classes and single-use versus multi-use formulations were evaluated. Medication use in Sjögren syndrome-associated versus non-Sjögren DED was compared using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age and sex.

Main outcome measures

Annual treated DED prevalence, medication prescribing proportions, formulation-specific prescribing trends, and differences between Sjögren syndrome-associated and non-Sjögren syndrome DED.

Results

Approximately 61.8 million patient-years were analyzed, representing 9.87 million unique patients. Annual treated DED prevalence ranged from 4.84% to 5.61% and was consistently higher in women and older individuals. Hyaluronic acid (HA) remained the most prescribed medication, although its proportional share declined from 85.03% in 2014 to 76.89% in 2023 (P < .001). Diquafosol prescriptions increased from 4.61% to 10.77%, and cyclosporine prescriptions increased from 2.39% to 5.77% (both P < .001). Single-use HA prescriptions increased from 39.73% to 73.76% (P < .001), and single-use diquafosol accounted for 61.8% of diquafosol prescriptions by 2023. Cyclosporine was prescribed to 26.00% of patients with Sjögren syndrome-associated DED and 7.51% of those with non-Sjögren DED; the adjusted OR was 4.06 (95% CI, 3.99-4.12).

Conclusions

Over the past decade, DED management in Korea shifted toward the anti-inflammatory cyclosporine, the mucin and water secretagogue diquafosol, and preservative-free single-use formulations. Patients with Sjögren syndrome-associated DED demonstrated distinct prescribing patterns, including substantially greater cyclosporine use after adjustment for age and sex.

records.title: Validation of the University of California, Irvine Corneal Cystine Crystal Score (UCI CCCS): Correlations with Clinical, Imaging, and Symptom Outcomes in Cystinosis.

content.title: Validation of the University of California, Irvine Corneal Cystine Crystal Score (UCI CCCS): Correlations with Clinical, Imaging, and Symptom Outcomes in Cystinosis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To prospectively validate the University of California, Irvine Corneal Cystine Crystal Score (UCI CCCS), a standardized slit-lamp grading tool, by evaluating associations with objective corneal densitometry, patient-reported symptoms, and visual acuity in a real-world cystinosis cohort.

Design

Prospective observational cross-sectional study.

Participants

Seventy patients (140 eyes) with confirmed cystinosis were examined at the 2024-2025 Cystinosis Research Foundation Day of Hope Clinics.

Methods

All eyes underwent live slit-lamp UCI CCCS grading (0-5). Pentacam Scheimpflug densitometry was obtained in 68 eyes. Two ophthalmologists independently graded patients during the 2025 clinic to assess inter-rater reliability. Patient-reported symptoms, best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), and topical cysteamine treatment data were collected. Linear mixed-effects models accounting for within-patient correlation were used for densitometry and BCVA analyses. Symptom associations were evaluated at the patient level using Kendall's tau-b.

Main outcome measures

Inter-rater reliability of UCI CCCS; associations with corneal densitometry, patient-reported symptoms, and BCVA.

Results

Inter-rater reliability was excellent (ICC = 0.995; 95% CI, 0.992-0.996). Linear mixed-effects modeling demonstrated significant associations between UCI CCCS grade and central (p = 0.0016) and anterior corneal densitometry (p = 0.0011) after accounting for within-patient correlation between fellow eyes. Higher UCI CCCS grades were significantly associated with greater photophobia (τ = 0.397, p < 0.0001), foreign-body sensation (τ = 0.295, p = 0.0047), and ocular dryness (τ = 0.405, p = 0.0001). No statistically significant association was observed between UCI CCCS grade and BCVA after accounting for within-patient correlation (p = 0.4389). No significant differences in UCI CCCS or corneal densitometry were observed across topical cysteamine treatment groups.

Conclusion

The UCI CCCS is a highly reproducible, clinically practical grading tool associated with objective corneal densitometry and patient-reported symptom burden, while BCVA was not significantly associated with UCI CCCS grade. Longitudinal studies are needed to evaluate treatment responsiveness and prognostic value.

records.title: Cytopathology and Prognostic Accuracy of 15-GEP/PRAME: The Collaborative Ocular Oncology Group Study 2.

content.title: Cytopathology and Prognostic Accuracy of 15-GEP/PRAME: The Collaborative Ocular Oncology Group Study 2.
content.abstract:
Importance

Gene expression profiling (GEP) reliably predicts metastatic uveal melanoma risk and is used to manage uveal melanoma (UM) in patients with this diagnosis. Efforts to refine molecular prognostication continue.

Objective

To determine if confirmatory cytopathology findings influence the prognostic accuracy of a commercially available GEP/Preferentially Expressed Antigen in Melanoma (PRAME) assay.

Design, setting, and participants

The Collaborative Ocular Oncology Group 2 study, a prospective cohort study, was conducted from 2017 to 2020 with follow-up recorded at 6-month intervals. This was a multicenter study that included patients with choroidal and/or ciliary body melanoma and results from a 15-GEP and PRAME RNA expression (15-GEP/PRAME) assay. Patients with iris tumors or less than 6 months' follow-up were excluded. Study data were analyzed from April 2025 to July 2026.

Exposures

15-GEP/PRAME, cytopathology, and next-generation sequencing (NGS).

Main outcomes and measures

Metastatic uveal melanoma rates in patients who had 15-GEP/PRAME and confirmatory cytopathology (CCP) results confirming or suspicious for UM (GEP+CCP) were compared with those who had 15-GEP/PRAME and no cytopathology performed, or unknown or nondiagnostic cytopathology results (GEP only). UM-associated variants identified by NGS were also evaluated.

Results

Of 1537 patients (mean [SD] age, 62.0 [13.4] years; 787 male [51.2%]), 727 (47.3%) had CCP results, and 810 (52.7%) had nondiagnostic cytopathology results or no cytopathology performed. Class 2/PRAME+ tumors were more common (136 of 727 [18.7%]) in the GEP+CCP group than in the GEP-only group (72 of 810 [8.9%]; 9.8% difference; 95% CI, 6.4-13.3; P <.001), whereas class 1/PRAME- tumors were less common (330 of 727 [45.4%] vs 495 of 810 [61.1%]; 15.7% difference; 95% CI, 10.8-20.6; P <.001). In patients with GEP+CCP, 22.7% (n = 165) developed metastasis vs 15.4% (n = 125) in patients with GEP only (7.3% difference, 95% CI, 3.3-11.2; P < .001). Adjusting for 15-GEP/PRAME status, there were no differences in metastasis rates between CCP groups. Of 1327 patients with successful NGS, 94.1% (605 of 643) in the GEP+CCP group and 71.9% (492 of 684) in the GEP-only group had a UM-associated variant (22.2% difference, 95% CI, 18.3-26.0; P < .001).

Conclusions and relevance

Results of this cohort study reveal that no differences in metastasis outcomes were observed between patients with and without CCP within any GEP/PRAME categories. UM-associated variants were found less frequently in the GEP-only group than in the GEP+CCP group. In this cohort, 15-GEP/PRAME classification without CCP retained prognostic validity, supporting its clinical consideration in guiding metastatic surveillance in cases in which cytopathology is unavailable.

records.title: STRUCTURE-FUNCTION ASSOCIATION BETWEEN CONTRAST SENSITIVITY FUNCTION AND OPTICAL COHERENCE TOMOGRAPHY FEATURES IN PATIENTS WITH IDIOPATHIC EPIRETINAL MEMBRANE.

content.title: STRUCTURE-FUNCTION ASSOCIATION BETWEEN CONTRAST SENSITIVITY FUNCTION AND OPTICAL COHERENCE TOMOGRAPHY FEATURES IN PATIENTS WITH IDIOPATHIC EPIRETINAL MEMBRANE.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Investigate the structure-function relationships between epiretinal membrane (ERM) stage, tractional abnormalities, and the gap area between the ERM and the retinal surface, in relation to visual acuity and quantitative contrast sensitivity function in patients with idiopathic epiretinal membrane.

Methods

This was a retrospective, cross-sectional study involving 111 participants diagnosed with idiopathic ERM. All patients underwent a comprehensive ophthalmologic examination, spectral-domain optical coherence tomography imaging using the SPECTRALIS Heidelberg system, and contrast sensitivity (CS) testing using the quantitative contrast sensitivity function method.

Results

Progressive stages of ERM were associated with declines in both CS and visual acuity (β* = -0.45 to -0.19, P < 0.02), with CS showing a more pronounced reduction than visual acuity, especially between controls and Stage 1. Ectopic inner foveal layer thickness exhibited a similar pattern of decline in both visual acuity (β* = 0.42, P < 0.001) and CS (β* = -0.46 to -0.18, all P < 0.02). By contrast, SUKIMA showed no significant association with any of the visual measurements assessed. Among the tractional abnormalities, the cotton ball sign correlated with diminished vision, particularly reflected by a notable drop in CS at the highest spatial frequencies tested with reduced CS at 12 cycles per degree (β* = -0.44, P = 0.02) and 18 cycles per degree (β* = -0.46, P = 0.02).

Conclusion

Quantitative contrast sensitivity function testing is particularly important for assessing visual function in ERM development, especially in the early stages.

records.title: Longitudinal Changes in Scleral Thickness after Half-dose Photodynamic Therapy in Central Serous Chorioretinopathy.

content.title: Longitudinal Changes in Scleral Thickness after Half-dose Photodynamic Therapy in Central Serous Chorioretinopathy.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate longitudinal changes in scleral thickness after half-dose photodynamic therapy (PDT) in eyes with central serous chorioretinopathy (CSC) in parallel with widefield assessment of choroidal thickness.

Methods

This retrospective observational study included 41 eyes of 41 patients with unilateral CSC who underwent half-dose PDT for persistent subretinal fluid and completed 12 months of follow-up. Scleral thickness was measured in 4 quadrants using anterior-segment optical coherence tomography (OCT) at baseline and at 3 and 12 months after PDT. Widefield choroidal thickness was assessed using widefield swept-source OCT with an 18-mm grid divided into 9 sectors. Untreated fellow eyes served as a reference group.

Results

In treated eyes, widefield choroidal thickness decreased significantly at 3 months after PDT across all 9 predefined sectors (all P < 0.05) and remained reduced at 12 months, with no significant differences between 3 and 12 months. In untreated fellow eyes, no consistent longitudinal changes in choroidal thickness were observed; however, a statistically significant reduction was noted only in the outer superonasal sector at 3 months (P = 0.015). In contrast, scleral thickness showed no significant changes at any time point in either treated or fellow eyes (all P > 0.05).

Conclusions

Despite widespread and sustained choroidal thinning after half-dose PDT, scleral thickness remained unchanged for at least 12 months in eyes with CSC. These findings suggest that scleral thickening in CSC is unlikely to represent a readily reversible response to treatment-associated choroidal changes and may instead reflect a relatively stable anatomical feature.

records.title: EFFECTIVENESS AND SAFETY OF BIOSIMILAR ANTIVASCULAR ENDOTHELIAL GROWTH FACTOR FOR RETINAL DISEASES: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: EFFECTIVENESS AND SAFETY OF BIOSIMILAR ANTIVASCULAR ENDOTHELIAL GROWTH FACTOR FOR RETINAL DISEASES: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the comparative effectiveness and safety of biosimilar antivascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) versus reference anti-VEGF intravitreal injections for the treatment of retinal diseases.

Methods

A systematic review and meta-analysis was performed on studies identified through searches of Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library between January 2015 and September 2024. Studies evaluating effectiveness and/or safety outcomes of biosimilar anti-VEGF were included. Meta-analysis was performed with a random-effects model. Risk of bias assessment was performed with the Joanna Briggs Institute tools, and certainty of evidence was evaluated with the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation criteria.

Results

A total of 25 studies were included in the meta-analysis. Diagnoses studied were neovascular age-related macular degeneration, diabetic macular edema, retinal vein occlusion, and polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy. There were no significant differences in final visual acuity, change in visual acuity, final retinal thickness, change in retinal thickness, and incidence of adverse events over a follow-up duration of 12 to 63.6 weeks. Subgroup analyses of randomized controlled trials, observational studies, age-related macular degeneration, diabetic macular edema, and agent-specific analysis (aflibercept and ranibizumab) were not significant. Findings are supported by evidence of moderate to high certainty as per the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation tool. There was a low to moderate risk of bias in the included study as per the Joanna Briggs Institute tools.

Conclusion

Biosimilar anti-VEGF is comparable with reference anti-VEGF regarding safety profile and visual outcomes. Future research should prioritize including diverse patient populations and adopting standardized, extended follow-up periods to enhance the assessment of long-term safety and effectiveness of biosimilars.

records.title: Biologic Switching Strategies for Anti-Tumor Necrosis Factor Alpha Refractory Noninfectious Uveitis: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Clinical Approach.

content.title: Biologic Switching Strategies for Anti-Tumor Necrosis Factor Alpha Refractory Noninfectious Uveitis: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Clinical Approach.
content.abstract:
Topic

This study aimed to investigate switching strategies of biologics in noninfectious uveitis (NIU) refractory to anti-tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNFα) agents.

Clinical relevance

Noninfectious uveitis often requires biologic therapy when conventional immunosuppression fails. Tumor necrosis factor alpha inhibitors, such as adalimumab and infliximab, are commonly used as first-line biologics, but up to one-third of patients experience inadequate responses.

Methods

We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate clinical outcomes following biologic switching in patients with NIU refractory to anti-TNFα therapy. This review was registered at PROSPERO (CRD420251071702). PubMed, EMBASE, and Cochrane Library were searched through January 5, 2025. Switching strategies were categorized as either intraclass (switching between anti-TNFα agents) or interclass (switching from an anti-TNFα agent to a different class biologic). Pooled response rates were compared between the two approaches. Risk of bias was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) checklists for case reports/series and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale for comparative studies. Certainty of evidence for primary outcome was evaluated using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation approach.

Results

A total of 136 studies (129 case reports/series and 7 comparative studies) were included for systematic review, with 89 studies contributing to the meta-analysis. Using the JBI tool, 11 of 77 studies had high risk of bias, while the remainder were of at least fair quality. Among comparative studies, one-third had moderate risk of bias, while the rest were rated as low risk. The overall pooled response rate after switching was 83% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 76%-90%; I2 = 30.2%; 466 patients). Intraclass switching showed a pooled response rate of 77% (95% CI: 65%-87%; I2 = 36%), which was lower than that of interclass switching showing 89% (95% CI: 80%-96%; I2 = 18%, P = 0.0995). Sensitivity analyses showed a 71% (95% CI: 59%-82%, I2 = 54.5%) pooled response rate for intraclass switch and 85% (95% CI: 77%-93%, I2 = 32.8%) for interclass switch, revealing statistically significant difference (P = 0.044). The certainty of evidence was graded as low for the overall pooled response rate after switching.

Conclusions

Both intraclass and interclass switching strategies appear effective, with interclass switching showing higher response rates; however, these findings warrant cautious interpretation given the limited certainty of evidence.

records.title: THERAPEUTICS FOR MANAGEMENT OF PROLIFERATIVE VITREORETINOPATHY RELATED TO RHEGMATOGENOUS RETINAL DETACHMENT: A Network Meta-Analysis.

content.title: THERAPEUTICS FOR MANAGEMENT OF PROLIFERATIVE VITREORETINOPATHY RELATED TO RHEGMATOGENOUS RETINAL DETACHMENT: A Network Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare the efficacy and safety of adjunctive therapies for proliferative vitreoretinopathy (PVR) related to rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD).

Methods

A systematic literature search was conducted on Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) from January 2000 to December 2025. A Bayesian random-effects network meta-analysis was used to compare different therapies.

Results

A total of 2,519 patients from 18 RCTs were included (1,339 receiving adjunctive treatments and 1,180 receiving placebo). Oral retinoic acid was associated with significantly higher primary (hazard ratio [HR] = 2.86, 95% CI = [1.16, 7.53]) and final (HR = 2.90, 95% CI = [1.12, 7.50]) retinal reattachment rates, improved visual acuity (MD=-0.89, 95% CI = [-1.68, -0.08]), and a lower incidence of postoperative macular pucker (HR = 0.12, 95% CI = [0.02, 0.50]) compared with placebo. Oral prednisolone had a lower rate of PVR recurrence compared with placebo (HR = 0.37, 95% CI = [0.17, 0.79]), while oral retinoic acid (HR = 0.06, 95% CI = [0.00, 0.50]) and intravitreal dexamethasone (HR = 0.23, 95% CI = [0.05, 0.81]) were associated with reduced rates of RRD reoperation.

Conclusion

Oral retinoic acid ranked highest for primary outcomes in PVR associated with RRD; however, this finding was driven by a single RCT with limited sample size. Oral prednisolone reduced PVR recurrence, while intravitreal dexamethasone lowered reoperation risk, compared with placebo.

records.title: Incidence and Progression of Glaucoma Following Boston Type 1 Keratoprosthesis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Incidence and Progression of Glaucoma Following Boston Type 1 Keratoprosthesis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Topic

Boston Type 1 Keratoprosthesis (KPro) implantation is an established surgery for severe corneal blindness when traditional keratoplasty is not feasible. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to quantify the incidence and progression of glaucoma following KPro implantation.

Clinical relevance

Despite advances in device design and postoperative management, glaucoma remains a sight-threatening complication. Accurate estimates of glaucoma incidence and progression can inform treatment decisions and enhance long-term visual outcomes in this high-risk population.

Methods

MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL were systematically searched from inception to June 2025. Two independent reviewers performed title/abstract screening, full-text screening, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment, with discrepancies resolved through discussion with a third reviewer. Studies reporting glaucoma-related outcomes following KPro implantation were included. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed to estimate pooled incidences of postoperative glaucoma. Risk of bias was assessed using Joanna Briggs Institute tools, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE. This review was prospectively registered on PROSPERO (ID: CRD420251036643).

Results

Twenty-three studies met inclusion criteria, encompassing 1,482 eyes with a mean follow-up of 39.4 months (±14.4). The mean patient age was 54.5 years (±8.9). Pre-existing glaucoma affected 45.9% of eyes. Overall, the pooled incidence of any form of postoperative glaucoma events was 25.6% (95% CI: 18.1-34.8%, I² = 87.3%) and an incidence rate of 0.09 events per eye-year (95% CI: 0.07-0.13; I² = 91.6%). Among studies explicitly reporting de novo glaucoma, the pooled incidence was 31.1% (95% CI: 20.6-43.9%, I² = 70.6%), while progression of pre-existing glaucoma occurred in 37.7% of eyes (95% CI: 17.9-62.6%, I² = 85.7%). Ocular hypertension without diagnostic confirmation of glaucoma was observed in 17.1% of eyes (95% CI: 5.6-41.9%, I² = 71.3%). Significant heterogeneity was observed across studies, stemming from variability in outcome definitions, indication for KPro, and reporting practices.

Conclusions

Glaucoma represents a clinically important complication following KPro implantation, affecting approximately one-quarter to one-third of eyes postoperatively. Although the certainty of evidence is very low due to heterogeneity and variability in diagnostic definitions, the results underscore the need for vigilant perioperative monitoring and standardized diagnostic approaches.

records.title: Diagnostic Accuracy and Complementary Value of Biomarkers for Primary Vitreoretinal Lymphoma: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

content.title: Diagnostic Accuracy and Complementary Value of Biomarkers for Primary Vitreoretinal Lymphoma: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the individual and combined diagnostic performance of cytokine, molecular, and clonality biomarkers for primary vitreoretinal lymphoma (PVRL).

Design

Systematic review and meta-analysis.

Participants

A total of 2411 patients from 41 studies with confirmed PVRL or benign ocular inflammatory diseases.

Methods

Prospectively registered (CRD420251265910). Four databases were searched through November 25, 2025. Methodologic quality was assessed using QUADAS-2 and Comparative tools. Diagnostic accuracy was pooled using hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic (HSROC) models with GRADE certainty assessment.

Main outcome measures

Pooled sensitivity, specificity, and AUSROC for each biomarker with GRADE certainty ratings.

Results

Of 41 included studies, most were rated at high or unclear risk of bias across Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies 2 domains, predominantly in patient selection because of retrospective designs and nonconsecutive sampling, and in the index test domain because of post hoc threshold selection. The interleukin (IL)-10 to IL-6 ratio (27 studies; 1370 patients; AUSROC, 0.98; sensitivity, 0.89; specificity, 0.98; I2 = 61% and 69%, respectively; low certainty) showed no publication bias. MYD88 (12 studies; 382 patients; AUSROC, 0.89; sensitivity, 0.73, specificity, 0.99; I2 = 37% and 68%, respectively; very low certainty), IGH (12 studies; 649 patients; AUSROC, 0.97; sensitivity, 0.85, specificity, 0.97; I2 = 80% and 87%, respectively; very low certainty), and IL-10 alone (11 studies; 549 patients; AUSROC, 0.94; sensitivity, 0.87, specificity, 0.95; I2 = 58% and 84%, respectively; low certainty) did not outperform IL-10 and IL-6 statistically. CD79B (4 studies; 123 patients; AUSROC, 1.00; sensitivity, 0.40; specificity, 1.00; I2 = 35% and 0%, respectively; low certainty) showed numerically higher accuracy (P = 0.055). Parallel testing of IL-10 to IL-6 ratio and MYD88 achieved 97.1% sensitivity and 97.0% specificity, reducing false-negative rates from 11% to 2.9%.

Conclusions

Parallel testing of IL-10 to IL-6 ratio and MYD88 seemed to offer the highest diagnostic performance among evaluated strategies for PVRL, although this finding requires prospective validation given the low to very low certainty of the underlying evidence. Aqueous humor cytokine testing yielded higher diagnostic odds ratios than vitreous fluid, suggesting anterior paracentesis for IL-10 to IL-6 ratio before vitreous biopsy for molecular confirmation.

Financial disclosure(s)

The author(s) have no proprietary or commercial interest in any materials discussed in this article.

records.title: Intraocular Pressure Changes Following Intraluminal Stent Removal From the Paul Glaucoma Implant: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Intraocular Pressure Changes Following Intraluminal Stent Removal From the Paul Glaucoma Implant: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

This study aims to systematically review and perform a single-arm meta-analysis to comprehensively evaluate the effect of removal of intraluminal stent from the Paul glaucoma implant (PGI) on intraocular pressure (IOP) changes and to summarize its long-term efficacy and safety.

Clinical relevance

Glaucoma remains one of the leading global causes of irreversible vision loss, necessitating effective surgical management for refractory cases. Glaucoma drainage devices are critical for these complex forms, and intraluminal stent removal from the PGI serves as a key strategy to titrate aqueous outflow and optimize long-term IOP control.

Methods

A systematic review was conducted by searching EMBASE, Medline, and CENTRAL. The meta-analysis ultimately included 5 observational studies. The Risk of Bias in Nonrandomized Studies of Interventions (ROBINS-I) tool was used to assess the quality of the included studies. Continuous outcomes (eg, postremoval stent IOP reduction) were analyzed using the mean difference (MD) with 95% confidence intervals (CI); dichotomous outcomes (eg, hypotony incidence) were evaluated using pooled proportion with 95% CI. All meta-analyses employed a random-effects model.

Results

Our meta-analysis included 5 studies, involving a total of 283 eyes. The meta-analysis revealed that removal of the stent leads to a significant and immediate IOP reduction. The IOP reduction (immediate postremoval stent IOP minus preremoval stent IOP) was significant, with a pooled MD of -9.09 mm Hg IOP (MD = 9.09; 95% CI = [-11.77, -6.41]). In the preremoval stent high-IOP (>21 mm Hg) subgroup, the IOP reduction is -11.82 (95% CI = [-10.14, -13.51]). This reduction was significantly greater than the preremoval stent low-IOP (<21 mm Hg) subgroup, whose reduction is -6.66 mm Hg (95% CI = [-5.55, -7.77]). Regarding safety, the pooled proportion of clinically hypotony was low and highly consistent (I² = 0.00%) at only 0.03 (95% CI = [0.00, 0.15]).

Conclusions

Intraluminal stent removal from the PGI is an effective and safe IOP-lowering intervention. Its IOP reduction effect is significantly more pronounced in patients with preremoval stent high IOP, providing crucial clinical guidance for managing persistently high IOP after PGI implantation.

records.title: ASSOCIATION BETWEEN ANTIBIOTIC PROPHYLAXIS AND ENDOPHTHALMITIS AFTER INTRAVITREAL INJECTION: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: ASSOCIATION BETWEEN ANTIBIOTIC PROPHYLAXIS AND ENDOPHTHALMITIS AFTER INTRAVITREAL INJECTION: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare the incidence of endophthalmitis after intravitreal injection with versus without topical antibiotic prophylaxis.

Methods

We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from each database's inception through August 2024. The primary outcome measure was the endophthalmitis rates after intravitreal injection, whereas the secondary outcomes included the distribution and quantity of microorganisms and best-corrected visual acuity changes. Study quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. For the meta-analysis, pooled summary estimates were calculated using a random-effects model.

Results

Eighteen studies (3,138,778 intravitreal injections; 1,426 endophthalmitis cases) showed no significant difference in endophthalmitis incidence between prophylaxis and no-prophylaxis groups (odds ratio 1.85, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.72‒4.76; P = 0.2). For microbial analysis, we selected 11 studies that demonstrated no significant difference in culture-positive rates between prophylaxis and nonprophylaxis groups (OR, 1.23; 95% CI, [0.53‒2.84]; P = 0.63). Four studies provided best-corrected visual acuity changes from baseline to final follow-up, antibiotic prophylaxis group showed a decrease by 4.5 ETDRS letters compared with the no-prophylaxis group, although this difference was not statistically significant ( P = 0.65).

Conclusion

Topical antibiotics did not reduce endophthalmitis risk or improve visual outcomes postintravitreal injection. Given potential risks, routine prophylaxis is not recommended.

records.title: Clinical and Multimodal Imaging Findings in Extensive Macular Atrophy With Pseudodrusen (EMAP): A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Clinical and Multimodal Imaging Findings in Extensive Macular Atrophy With Pseudodrusen (EMAP): A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Topic

This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to integrate the clinical and multimodal imaging features of extensive macular atrophy associated with pseudodrusen (EMAP), and to evaluate its progression and associated risk factors.

Clinical relevance

EMAP is a retinal disorder with a distinct phenotype and poor visual prognosis that typically affects patients in their middle age. There is no standardized classification for EMAP nor a clear understanding of its etiology. Identifying clinical and imaging biomarkers is critical to improve EMAP diagnosis and guiding future research.

Methods

We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis following PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO, CRD42024474924). A comprehensive literature search of MEDLINE, EMBASE, Web of Science, and ClinicalTrials.gov was performed up to June 19, 2025. Randomized and nonrandomized studies of EMAP were eligible. Meta-analyses were performed using random-effects models. Heterogeneity was assessed with the I2 statistic, and risk of bias by the NOS. The examined outcomes were disease symptoms, best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), progression of macular atrophy, imaging biomarkers, and systemic associations. EMAP was diagnosed using multimodal imaging analysis.

Results

Sixteen studies met the inclusion criteria for qualitative analysis, and 12 datasets were included (N = 1096 eyes). The mean BCVA at diagnosis was 0.62 logMAR (95% CI: 0.47-0.76; I² = 95.6%), with a mean worsening of 0.41 logMAR (3 lines of vision) over 2.1 years. Disease progression involved an increase in the macular atrophy area by an average of 8.3 mm² over 3.9 years (95% CI: 3-3.57; I² = 69.8%). Optical coherence tomography showed a mean central choroidal thickness of 135.8 (95% CI: 113.3-158.3; I² = 94.4%). Electroretinography data indicated a rod dysfunction with abnormal photopic response. Rheumatic fever was reported in 89% of patients across Brazilian cohorts (95% CI: 83.2-93; I² = 0%).

Conclusions

This meta-analysis has limitations, mostly due to heterogeneity and biases inherent to non-randomized studies of this disease, hence the inconsistencies in the results and hypothesized associations underlying EMAP. Despite the different imaging modalities used to diagnose EMAP, the results demonstrate the common features that characterize and support its diagnosis.

records.title: Rate and Risk of Nonarteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy with Semaglutide Use for Diabetes and Weight Loss: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Rate and Risk of Nonarteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy with Semaglutide Use for Diabetes and Weight Loss: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Topic

This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates the rate and risk of nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION) in adults receiving semaglutide for diabetes or weight loss.

Clinical relevance

Semaglutide is a transformative treatment for diabetes and obesity. Nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy is a serious cause of sudden, often permanent, vision loss. A comprehensive synthesis of available and conflicting evidence of a potential link is needed to inform clinical practice.

Methods

Our comprehensive search included MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, clinical trial registries, and direct contact with trial sponsors to identify unpublished data from inception to March 2025. We included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational studies evaluating semaglutide versus placebo or standard therapy in adults. Incident NAION was the primary outcome. Pooled incidence rates, hazard ratios (HRs), and risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using random-effects models, uniquely stratified by both clinical indication (diabetes/weight loss) and study design.

Results

Our search identified 8 RCTs (31 174 patients, including 3 RCTs not previously synthesized in meta-analyses) and 8 observational studies (1 611 278 patients) were included. Observational studies for diabetes showed a pooled NAION incidence of 26.7 per 100 000 person-years in those on semaglutide versus 18.9 per 100 000 person-years in those not on semaglutide (HR 1.85, 95% CI 1.20-2.85). Randomized controlled trials for diabetes demonstrated 5 ischemic optic neuropathy events in those on semaglutide versus one in those not, with no significant evidence of increased risk (RR 1.76, 95% CI 0.43-7.25). Observational studies of semaglutide for weight loss showed no evidence of increased NAION hazards (HR 1.57, 95% CI 0.69-3.59), and RCTs (4 ION events vs one) found no evidence of increased risk (RR 2.18, 95% CI 0.33-14.34).

Conclusion

The absolute rate of NAION in semaglutide users is low. Our novel, stratified analysis provides a more nuanced interpretation than previous pooled reviews, isolating a potential increased risk signal to observational data in the diabetes population only, a finding not corroborated by RCTs. The comprehensiveness of our search and rigorous sensitivity analyses to account for patient overlap in databases strengthen the validity of these conclusions. This synthesis highlights the need for continued pharmacovigilance while contextualizing the low absolute risk.

records.title: Clinical Efficacy of Biosimilar Switch of Adalimumab and Infliximab for Noninfectious Uveitis: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Clinical Efficacy of Biosimilar Switch of Adalimumab and Infliximab for Noninfectious Uveitis: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the clinical efficacy of switching from originator tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) inhibitors to biosimilars in the management of noninfectious uveitis.

Design

A systematic review and meta-analysis.

Methods

A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted on PubMed, Embase, and Scopus according to PRISMA guidelines and registered on PROSPERO (ID: CRD420251051301). Studies were included if they reported outcomes related to uveitis control, including flare frequency, oral corticosteroid use, or nonbiologic immunomodulatory therapy (IMT) use, before and after switching. Meta-analyses were performed to compare the incidence rate ratio (IRR) of uveitis flares, as well as the risk ratios (RR) of oral corticosteroid and nonbiological IMT use, before and after switching.

Results

A total of 6 studies were included, with publication dates ranging from 2019 to 2024. The studies included a total of 202 patients that underwent an originator to biosimilar switch. The pooled IRR of uveitis flares postswitch was 1.26 (95% CI: 0.72-2.21, P = 0.411), with significant heterogeneity (P = 0.08). Heterogeneity could be resolved through a secondary analysis excluding flares occurring within 3 months postswitch, due to early flare clustering reported in 1 study, that found an IRR of 1.20 (95% CI: 0.79-1.83, P = 0.388) without heterogeneity (P = .25). There was no significant change in the risk of oral steroid use (RR = 1.00; 95% CI: 0.88-1.12, P = 0.944) or nonbiologic IMT use (RR = 0.98; 95% CI 0.83-1.16, P = .858) postswitch. A total of 30 patients (Pooled Proportions = 0.10; 95% CI: 0.041-0.219, P = 0.022) reverted to the originator agent, most commonly due to injection-site pain or technical difficulties with the biosimilar injector.

Conclusions

Switching from originator to biosimilar TNF-α inhibitors in noninfectious uveitis was not associated with an increase in flare rates, supporting the clinical equivalence of these biosimilars. However, a subset of patients may experience tolerability issues or early flares, warranting close monitoring in the months following a switch.

records.title: Outcomes of Penetrating Keratoplasty and Boston Type 1 Keratoprosthesis in Aniridia-Associated Keratopathy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Outcomes of Penetrating Keratoplasty and Boston Type 1 Keratoprosthesis in Aniridia-Associated Keratopathy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Congenital aniridia is a rare condition, which may lead to aniridia-associated keratopathy (AAK) and corneal blindness. Our objective was to compare the surgical outcomes of penetrating keratoplasty (PK) and Boston type 1 keratoprosthesis (KPro) implantation in patients with AAK.

Design

Systematic review and meta-analysis of individual patient data (IPD).

Methods

The study was preregistered in the PROSPERO database (registration number: CRD420250650812). A comprehensive search of Embase, MEDLINE (via PubMed), and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) was performed up to February 17, 2025. Eligible studies reported clinical outcomes after PK or KPro in patients with AAK, specifically graft survival, success rates, best spectacle-corrected visual acuity (BSCVA), and postoperative complications. Data extraction and synthesis followed the Cochrane Handbook, and risk of bias was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklists.

Results

Of the 1,590 studies screened, 26 case series comprising 325 eyes with AAK were included in the meta-analysis. IPD were available from 14 studies. Anatomical success was significantly higher with KPro (0.82%, 95% CI: 0.65 to 0.92) than graft survival after PK (0.38%, 95% CI: 0.13 to 0.72) (P = .009). Cox regression analysis showed a significantly higher hazard of graft failure after PK compared to anatomical failure with KPro (HR = 2.92, 95% CI: 1.24 to 6.84; P = .014). No significant difference was observed in BSCVA improvement between PK (-0.73, 95% CI: -1.55 to 0.09) and KPro (-0.51, 95% CI: -0.82 to -0.20) (P = .48). Similarly, postoperative complication rates did not differ significantly between the two procedures (P = .62).

Conclusions

In patients with AAK, KPro shows superior anatomical success compared to graft survival following PK. Postoperative improvements in visual acuity and the incidence of complications do not differ significantly between the two procedures. The main limitations of this analysis are the relatively small sample size across studies, the limited duration of follow-up, and the heterogeneity of study designs.

records.title: Optical Coherence Tomography Predictive Biomarkers for Visual Outcomes after Macula-Off Rhegmatogenous Retinal Detachment: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Optical Coherence Tomography Predictive Biomarkers for Visual Outcomes after Macula-Off Rhegmatogenous Retinal Detachment: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Topic

Systematic review and meta-analysis of preoperative optical coherence tomography (OCT) features as predictors of visual outcomes following macula-off rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD) surgery.

Clinical relevance

To assess the impact of preoperatively assessed OCT parameters including photoreceptor ellipsoid zone (EZ) integrity, external limiting membrane (ELM) preservation, outer retinal corrugations (ORCs), subretinal fluid (SRF) height, intraretinal cysts (IRC), and epiretinal membrane (ERM) on post-operative best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA).

Methods

We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library databases through March 2025. Eligible studies evaluated preoperative OCT parameters as predictors of postoperative visual outcomes. Meta-analysis was performed using random-effects models with DerSimonian-Laird method to calculate pooled odds ratios (ORs) and standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Risk of bias for individual studies was assessed using a Modified Newcastle-Ottawa Quality Assessment Scale. The certainty of the body of evidence for each outcome was evaluated using the GRADE (Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation) approach.

Results

Twenty studies with 1841 eyes were included. Lower SRF height was associated with better outcomes (SMD: -0.72, 95% CI: -1.08 to -0.36; I² = 71%). Intact EZ was significantly associated with better visual outcomes (pooled OR: 3.76, 95% CI: 2.61-5.42; I² = 54%). Preserved ELM integrity was associated with better outcomes (pooled OR: 3.24, 95% CI: 2.13-4.92; I² = 49%). Absence of ORCs was associated with better outcomes (pooled OR: 2.83, 95% CI: 1.94-4.13; I² = 47%). Absence of IRC and ERM improved outcomes (OR: 2.26 and 2.64 respectively). SRF height predictive value was stronger for detachments ≤7 days. Morphologic staging systems showed strong correlation with visual outcomes (pooled r = 0.64, 95% CI: 0.52-0.74).

Conclusions

Based on low to very low-quality evidence according to GRADE assessment, preoperative OCT biomarkers may predict visual outcomes after macula-off RRD surgery, with photoreceptor layer integrity showing the strongest associations. However, the high heterogeneity, predominance of retrospective studies, and methodological limitations require that these findings be interpreted with significant caution and validated in high-quality prospective studies before clinical implementation.

records.title: Effectiveness and Safety of Cross-Linking in Keratoconus Patients With Corneal Thickness <400 µm: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

content.title: Effectiveness and Safety of Cross-Linking in Keratoconus Patients With Corneal Thickness <400 µm: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To investigate the effectiveness and safety of corneal cross-linking (CXL) in patients with keratoconus and thin corneas (corneal thickness <400 µm).

Design

Systematic review and meta-analysis.

Methods

MEDLINE Ovid, Embase Ovid, and Scopus were searched in July 2024 for studies published in peer-reviewed journals in English. Prospective and retrospective case series, cohort studies, and randomized clinical trials of people with corneal thickness of <400 µm (with or without epithelium) who underwent CXL for keratoconus were eligible, regardless of CXL approach. Key outcomes included maximum and mean corneal curvature (Kmax and Kmean), corrected and uncorrected distance visual acuity, refractive error, corneal thickness, and endothelial cell density at 3, 6, 12, and 24 months. Random effects meta-analysis was used to pool average change from preoperative values across CXL protocols. Study quality was assessed using the JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Case Series (PROSPERO registration: CRD42023403190).

Results

A total of 29 records published between 2011 and 2024 were included with a total of 470 eyes. Most studies were retrospective case series with substantial potential for bias. Substantial heterogeneity was observed between studies in terms of patients, CXL approach, and observed outcomes. At 12 months, flattening of the maximum corneal curvature (mean change in Kmax = -1.4 D, 95% CI = - 2.0, -0.9, n = 17/402 studies/eyes, I2= 93%) and improvement in corrected distance visual acuity (mean change = -0.09 logMAR units, 95% CI = - 0.13, -0.06], n = 19/443 studies/eyes, I2= 68%) were observed relative to baseline. No study reported major complications, and there were minimal reductions in corneal thickness and endothelial cell density.

Conclusions

Visual and keratometric parameters improved following CXL without major complications, suggesting that CXL may be suitable for patients with stromal thicknesses of <400 µm, providing that adequate modifications have been applied. Prospective comparative studies are required to guide the choice of approach.

records.title: An Agentic AI Workflow for Automated Macular Hole Diagnosis and Structured Report Generation.

content.title: An Agentic AI Workflow for Automated Macular Hole Diagnosis and Structured Report Generation.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Current AI models for optical coherence tomography (OCT) primarily focus on diagnosis as a standalone task. We developed and validated an end-to-end agentic AI workflow that integrates automated macular hole (MH) diagnosis from OCT images with structured patient-friendly report generation.

Methods

The proposed sequential workflow coordinated by a workflow orchestration agent consisted of an image diagnosis stage and a language generation step. The OCT version of RETFound, a self-supervised retinal foundation model, was fine-tuned for binary classification of macular OCT scans as MH or normal macula. Training, validation, and internal testing were performed using multiple public OCT datasets with patient-level stratified splitting, followed by external validation on two independent datasets. The performance of the fine-tuned foundation model was evaluated using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC AUC). For each new OCT image, the AI agent used the trained RETFound model to classify the image, received the diagnostic output, incorporated it into a structured prompt, and called the large language model (GPT-4) to generate the clinical report.

Results

On the internal test set (n = 180), the model achieved an accuracy of 100% (95% confidence interval (CI), 97.9-100%) with an AUC of 1.00. On external validation (n = 1014), accuracy was 98.8% (95% CI 97.9-99.3%), sensitivity was 97.9% (95% CI 96.3-98.8%), specificity was 100% (95% CI 99.2-100.0%), and AUC was 0.999 (95% CI 0.998-1.000). Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) analysis showed that predictions were driven by relevant retinal regions, particularly the macular hole and adjacent layers. The end-to-end agentic AI workflow generated concise and standardized patient-friendly reports for all samples, without the language model influencing diagnostic decisions.

Conclusions

This study demonstrates the feasibility of an end-to-end AI workflow coordinated by a workflow orchestration agent for robust OCT-based MH diagnosis with a large language model for structured report generation. By separating image-based diagnosis from language generation, this approach offers a practical and scalable solution for virtual vitreoretinal clinics.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Laser-Assisted Refractive Surgery-A Comprehensive Review.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Laser-Assisted Refractive Surgery-A Comprehensive Review.
content.abstract: Background/Objectives: Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology-in the form of Machine Learning (ML) models and other models specialized in image recognition and processing, such as Convolutional Neural Networks Visual Transformers (CNN-ViTs)-is increasingly being used in ophthalmology. This review summarizes the main AI applications for laser-assisted refractive surgery. Methods: A wide-ranging literature search on the PubMed and ISI Thompson Web of Science databases was conducted. Results: AI is an all-encompassing technological concept that refers to either specific applications of ML/CNN models, such as in keratoconus screening or diagnosis, or agentic/multimodal AI applications that process different data types using a variety of AI models. The most clinically established applications found were corneal ectasia and keratoconus screening, in which AI models can reliably exceed 95% diagnostic accuracy, specificity, and sensitivity; nomogram-derived laser ablation programming; optimization of ray-tracing calculations for ray-traced ablation profiles; patient screening and selection for refractive surgery; visual and refractive result prediction; assessment of postoperative corneal ectasia risk; detection of intraoperative complications; research on the laser coupling effect; and other applications such as monitoring eye rubbing behavior in corneal ectasia suspects. Thus, singular, specific applications of AI models have made the largest clinical contributions. These results must be interpreted with a comparison of internal versus external validation, calibration, and generalizability. Overall the technology is highly promising. Agentic/multimodal AI frameworks are currently being discussed, with pilot studies published and applicability proposed in the context of large, high-patient-volume clinical practices. The technological advent of SHAP force plot graphs and saliency maps has improved understanding of the factors that contribute mechanistically to AI model reasoning, leading to more informed clinical decisions or research applicability, such as in finding parameters or factors linked to postoperative ectasia. Conclusions: AI is already established in laser-assisted refractive surgery in the form of models specialized in data-intensive analysis. At present, the best-performing novel AI models originate from the domain of large or multi-hospital settings due to requirements for multiple latest-generation diagnostic devices, high-volume patient data, computing expertise, and resources. Future directions could include clinical standardization and trickle-down dissemination of the technology. Agentic/multimodal AI has the potential to benefit large clinical/patient settings or offer access to expert knowledge in smaller practice settings. Agentic/multimodal AI implementation is offset by challenges in complexity, the technological limitations of LLMs ("hallucinations"), and ethical and legislative factors.

records.title: Retinal Artificial Intelligence Reclassifies SCORE2-Based Cardiovascular Risk Across the ESC/EAS Statin-Indication Boundary: A UK Biobank Prospective Cohort Study.

content.title: Retinal Artificial Intelligence Reclassifies SCORE2-Based Cardiovascular Risk Across the ESC/EAS Statin-Indication Boundary: A UK Biobank Prospective Cohort Study.
content.abstract:
Aims

Whether a retinal artificial intelligence (AI) risk score reclassifies SCORE2 cardiovascular risk stratification in statin-naive adults across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary is uncertain. We evaluated the retinal AI risk score for 10-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) prediction.

Methods

In 40,672 statin-naive UK Biobank participants (aged 40-69, without diabetes), cardiovascular risk categories and treatment recommendation status (Class I or IIa vs neither) were defined using the 2025 ESC/EAS focused-update framework. Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) adjusted for SCORE2 or for established risk factors. The incremental predictive value of adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 was evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation.

Results

Over a 10.0-year median follow-up (914 ASCVD events), the very high retinal AI risk group independently predicted ASCVD (SCORE2-adjusted HR 2.32 vs low risk; p<0.001). Adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 reclassified risk across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary (statin-eligibility NRI [net reclassification improvement] 0.012, p<0.001); reclassification was statistically significant but modest (continuous NRI 0.445, p<0.001), without C-index or net-benefit gain. In the statin-indicated subgroup, retinal AI risk groups further stratified risk (SCORE2-adjusted HR 2.16; p<0.001). Statin-not-indicated participants in the high or very high retinal AI risk groups had numerically similar observed 10-year risk to all statin-indicated, untreated participants (p=0.758). There was no evidence of effect modification by clinically detectable retinal disorder (interaction p=0.93). Incremental value was greater in women than men (sex interaction p<0.001).

Conclusion

Adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 produced modest bidirectional risk reclassification across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary; these findings warrant prospective validation.Abstract word count: 250 words.

records.title: Automated Structured Reporting of Neurodegenerative Imaging Markers Using Quantitative MRI and Large Language Models.

content.title: Automated Structured Reporting of Neurodegenerative Imaging Markers Using Quantitative MRI and Large Language Models.
content.abstract:
Rationale and objectives

To evaluate the feasibility of a quantitative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-to-structured reporting pipeline that integrates quantitative MRI software with large language models (LLMs) for structured drafting of neurodegenerative imaging markers and generating clinician-facing report conclusions.

Materials and methods

A total of 192 patients with 3D T1 and 2D or 3D FLAIR MRI images from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative database were randomly selected. A deep-learning model generated structured report findings based on nine indices related to brain atrophy, white matter hyperintensities, and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) space abnormalities, and compared with neuroradiologist-generated reference reports. Four LLMs (GPT-OSS 20B, MedGemma 4B, Phi-3, and Llama 3.1 8B) generated clinician-facing conclusions from the structured findings. Generated conclusions were evaluated using a five-point Likert scale across four metrics (accuracy, relevance, clarity, and satisfaction). Output errors were assessed across four categories: language, omission, addition, and numeric errors.

Results

Structured report findings demonstrated high accuracy for CSF space analysis (77.6%-97.9%). Performance for ordinal visual scales was lower under strict matching (27.1%-57.8%) but improved with a one-grade tolerance (91.7%-97.4%). Among LLMs, GPT achieved the highest scores across most metrics (median score 5) and exhibited the lowest output error rates. Smaller models (Phi-3 and Llama 3.1 8B) showed overall lower performance, with more language, omission, and addition errors. MedGemma demonstrated intermediate performance, but the highest rate of numeric errors.

Conclusion

Our quantitative MRI-to-structured reporting pipeline, integrating quantitative MRI software with LLM-based conclusion generation, might be feasible for automated structured drafting of neurodegenerative imaging markers.

records.title: Empirical Evaluation of Post Hoc Interpretability Methods for Clinical Trust in Deep Learning Diagnostics.

content.title: Empirical Evaluation of Post Hoc Interpretability Methods for Clinical Trust in Deep Learning Diagnostics.
content.abstract: Background/Objectives: Brain tumor classification from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has been significantly improved through deep learning techniques; however, the lack of interpretability remains a major challenge for clinical adoption. Methods: This study proposes an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI)-driven framework for multiclass brain tumor classification using a baseline convolutional neural network (CNN) and four transfer learning models, namely ResNet50, DenseNet121, MobileNetV2, and EfficientNetB0. The models were trained and evaluated on a publicly available brain MRI dataset consisting of glioma, meningioma, and pituitary tumor classes. Their classification performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC), and confusion matrix analysis. To enhance transparency and interpretability, Grad-CAM, LIME, and SHAP were used to visualize and quantify the regions contributing to the classification decisions. Results: Experimental results state that the transfer learning models consistently outperformed the CNN by learning more discriminative feature representations while producing more localized and interpretable explanations. The agreement among Grad-CAM, LIME, and SHAP confirms that the proposed models predominantly relied on tumor regions rather than irrelevant background information, thereby improving the interpretability and reliability of the diagnostic predictions. Conclusions: The proposed framework provides an effective and explainable computer-aided diagnosis system that supports trustworthy deep learning-based brain tumor classification and has the potential for decision-making.

records.title: Accuracy and reproducibility of a large language model in assessing spirometry test acceptability and interpretation: a performance study.

content.title: Accuracy and reproducibility of a large language model in assessing spirometry test acceptability and interpretation: a performance study.
content.abstract:
Background

Spirometry is one of the most used pulmonary function tests for assessing respiratory function and diagnosing ventilatory disorders in clinical practice. Evaluation of test validity and interpretation is typically performed by trained healthcare professionals. The present study aims to evaluate the capability of a publicly available large language model (LLM) to perform quality assurance and interpretations of spirometry tests.

Methods

A total of 150 spirometry tests were retrospectively collected from the pulmonary function laboratories. The spirometry tests were evaluated for acceptability and interpreted by clinicians according to ATS/ERS recommendations as part of standard clinical practice. Subsequently, a publicly available LLM (ChatGPT 5.5) was prompted to evaluate the acceptability and interpret the same spirometry tests according to ATS/ERS criteria. The model interpreted each spirometry test on three separate occasions for assessing reproducibility. Accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV), with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), were calculated by comparing LLM assessments with clinician assessments of spirometry test acceptability and interpretation.

Results

For spirometry acceptability evaluation, ChatGPT demonstrated an overall accuracy of 87% (95% CI: 81%-92%), sensitivity of 91% (95% CI: 85%-95%), specificity of 61% (95% CI 39%-80%), PPV of 94% (95% CI: 89%-97%), and NPV of 48(95% CI: 29%-67%) with Cohen's k of 0.46. The spiromteric interpretation agreement with the clinicians reference standard was moderate, with exact agreement of 0.61 (95% CI: 0.54-0.69) while Cohen's Kappa (Unweighted) was 0.47 (95% CI: 0.37-0.56) and Macro F1 score was 0.39 (95% CI: 0.33-0.49). Reproducibility across three independent trials was moderate (Fleiss' κ 0.58). Class-specific interpretation performance varied by category; sensitivity was highest for normal pattern and restrictive defects (0.72), whereas sensitivity for obstructive defects was 0.27. F1-scores were highest for normal and restrictive defects (0.81 and 0.62, respectively).

Conclusion

The current findings suggest that ChatGPT 5.5 has a limited capability, at its current stage of development, to serve as a reliable tool for independent spirometry interpretation in clinical practice. Nevertheless, it may serve as an adjunct to clinical decision-making and educational tools. Prospective controlled studies are needed to confirm these findings.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment, and Perioperative Management: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment, and Perioperative Management: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives.
content.abstract:
Background

Breast cancer is the most frequently diagnosed malignancy in women globally, accounting for approximately 2.30 million new cases and 666,103 deaths in 2022. Artificial intelligence technologies including machine learning, deep learning, radiomics, and natural language processing have been widely applied across the breast cancer care continuum. However, no systematic review restricted to primary studies with patient-level or image-level data has synthesized evidence spanning all clinical domains simultaneously.

Objectives

To evaluate the performance, methodological quality, and clinical relevance of artificial intelligence primary studies across screening and diagnostic imaging, digital pathology, radiomics, perioperative management, prognostic prediction, and natural language processing in breast cancer.

Methods

PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from January 2015 to May 2026. Eligibility was restricted to original primary research reporting patient-level or image-level data; secondary syntheses were explicitly excluded. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2 and PROBAST. Reporting followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines.

Results

Of 5,275 identified records, 17 primary studies met eligibility criteria. In screening mammography (seven studies; n = 7,540 to 144,231 examinations), deep learning achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.876 to 0.939; a randomised trial in 80,033 women demonstrated non-inferiority to double reading with a 44.3% reduction in radiologist workload. In digital pathology (five studies; 270 to 44,732 whole-slide images), deep learning achieved AUC 0.985 to 0.994, exceeding unassisted pathologist performance in lymph node metastasis detection. Magnetic resonance imaging radiomics predicted pathological complete response in HER2-positive breast cancer with AUC 0.80. No breast cancer-specific perioperative primary study met the eligibility criteria. Deep survival networks achieved concordance index 0.626 versus 0.612 for Cox regression in breast cancer cohorts. Natural language processing identified metastatic recurrence in breast cancer clinical records with sensitivity 83% and specificity 73%. Risk of bias was low to moderate for imaging and pathology studies and high for small sample radiomics studies. Density-stratified performance was reported by only two imaging studies, and receptor status prediction from haematoxylin and eosin staining had not been validated as a safe alternative to immunohistochemistry.

Conclusions

Artificial intelligence demonstrated clinically meaningful performance across the five domains with eligible primary studies. Breast cancer-specific perioperative and intensive care primary studies were absent, representing the largest evidence gap. External validation, demographic diversity, and prospective clinical integration evidence remained the most consistently identified limitations. Prediction of molecular receptor status without immunohistochemistry requires rigorous prospective safety validation before it can complement standard testing.

records.title: Is Large Language Model a New Hope for the Global South? A Rapid Bibliometric Synthesis of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education.

content.title: Is Large Language Model a New Hope for the Global South? A Rapid Bibliometric Synthesis of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), especially the recent proliferation of generative Large Language Models (LLMs), is transforming traditional anatomy education by introducing new teaching tools. However, the adoption of these cutting-edge technologies raises questions about global educational equity. It remains unclear whether AI will serve as a digital equalizer or further exacerbate marginalization. This rapid bibliometric synthesis aims to provide a comprehensive, data-driven overview of the "Application of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education" (AAAE). We seek to map the intellectual landscape, detect structural and technological shifts, evaluate the geopolitical disparities, and provide corresponding references. A total of 85 consolidated records were retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus. These data constituted the whole panorama of AAAE. Bibliometrix and CiteSpace were utilized for static and dynamic mapping. A multidisciplinary expert panel validated the thematic clusters using Gwet's AC1 and the Normalized Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI). Publications surged following ChatGPT's release, indicating a shift from specialized computer vision to the application of general-purpose LLMs. While high-income countries maintain leadership, AI could exert a "democratizing effect" on upper-middle-income countries, doubling their odds of publication compared to traditional anatomy. Six research frontiers and three research trajectories were captured, and corresponding implications for future researchers in the global south and north were presented. AAAE could be conducted using a stratified strategy: different expansions of AI technologies for pedagogy; leveraging commercial APIs to bypass infrastructure bottlenecks; and validating open-source models. Global equity critically demands cross-border collaboration and inclusive datasets.

records.title: Applications of Artificial Intelligence-Driven Chatbots in University Level Dental Education: A Systematic Review.

content.title: Applications of Artificial Intelligence-Driven Chatbots in University Level Dental Education: A Systematic Review.
content.abstract:
Background

Artificial intelligence (AI), mainly AI-driven chatbots and large language models (LLMs) is reshaping dental education through adaptive, interactive, and simulation-based learning. While the transition in technology has been rapid, the evidence about the educational effectiveness of these technologies is still very diverse and not entirely directed.

Aim

To analyze the roles, educational effectiveness, and impact of integrating AI-driven chatbots and LLMs in dental education at the university level with a focus on learning outcomes and implementation practices.

Methods

The researchers conducted a thorough search of the electronic databases PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase for articles published from January 2018 to November 2025. This review met the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 criteria and was made up of original research articles on dental studentsand educators who were using AI-based chatbots as interventions. The outcomes measured were knowledge gain, clinical reasoning, diagnostic accuracy, communication skills, and engagement of learners. Due to the differences in the methodologies used the authors opted for a narrative synthesis approach.

Results

Six studies met the eligibility criteria and showed potential benefits of AI-driven chatbots and LLMs for diagnostic reasoning, learning performance, engagement, and individualized feedback although methodological and outcome heterogeneity limited direct comparison.

Conclusion

AI-driven chatbots and LLMs may complement university-level dental education, but their effectiveness and safe implementation require further rigorous evaluation.

records.title: Advancing Cancer Biomarker Discovery Through Multi-Omics, Bioinformatics, and Artificial Intelligence: A Systematic Review.

content.title: Advancing Cancer Biomarker Discovery Through Multi-Omics, Bioinformatics, and Artificial Intelligence: A Systematic Review.
content.abstract: The rapid accumulation of multi-omics data provides increasing opportunities for cancer biomarker discovery, but the heterogeneity and high dimensionality of these datasets remain major challenges for data integration and analysis. This review examines the application of bioinformatics and artificial intelligence for multi-omics integration in cancer biomarker research. Common multi-omics data paradigms and integration strategies are discussed, followed by a review of the bioinformatics, machine learning and deep learning approaches applied across 84 included studies. Cross-study comparison showed limited recurrence among the reported biomarkers, with only 15 biomarkers identified in at least four studies. Further assessment of the 13 recurrent protein-coding biomarkers showed significant protein-protein interaction enrichment and functional convergence in cancer-related processes, particularly PI3K/AKT and ERBB2-related signaling. This review also highlights current challenges, including missing data, heterogeneity across datasets, limited independent validation and the interpretability of artificial intelligence models. Future research may benefit from integrating multi-omics data with clinical information, pathological imaging, electronic health records, single-cell multi-omics and radiomics, together with broader datasets and greater use of independent validation to support the translation of multi-omics biomarker findings into clinical applications.

records.title: Experimental Protocols for Developing and Validating Explainable AI Models in Secure Healthcare Diagnostics.

content.title: Experimental Protocols for Developing and Validating Explainable AI Models in Secure Healthcare Diagnostics.
content.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has drastically enhanced healthcare diagnostics with automated disease detection, predictive analytics, and intelligent systems for clinical decision support. Nevertheless, the black-box nature of deep learning models hampers interpretability, clinical trust, and regulatory acceptance and raises concerns about data privacy and cybersecurity. This paper presents comprehensive experimental frameworks for developing and evaluating explainable AI models for secure healthcare diagnostics. The suggested model combines responsible data management, multimodal preprocessing, secure deep learning models, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods, and reproducible validation procedures in a single healthcare diagnostic pipeline. Methods of explaining, such as Grad-CAM, SHAP, LIME, and counterfactual analysis, were used to make the models more transparent and understandable for clinicians. At the same time, federated learning and differential privacy methods were used to securely manage highly sensitive patient data. Experimental evaluation has shown 96% classification accuracy, 94% sensitivity, and 95% specificity. These results were consistent in heterogeneous healthcare datasets. Compared to traditional black-box models, the explainability framework not only enhanced the interpretability of the results but also more accurately identified the regions relevant for diagnosis. Moreover, the secure federated learning architecture minimized privacy leakages without sacrificing the predictive performance and remained robust even when exposed to adversarial perturbations. An external evaluation also confirmed the reproducibility and generalizability of the protocols involved. This methodology offers a comprehensive and reliable foundation for deploying AI-powered diagnostics across multiple healthcare domains: radiology, pathology, oncology, cardiology, neurology, and precision medicine.

records.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Artificial Intelligence for Detecting ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction on 12-Lead Electrocardiograms: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Artificial Intelligence for Detecting ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction on 12-Lead Electrocardiograms: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) may improve electrocardiographic detection of ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), but available studies address distinct diagnostic questions. We systematically reviewed studies evaluating AI-based STEMI detection from 12-lead electrocardiograms and separately synthesized AI performance against a clinical reference standard, AI and clinician performance against a clinical reference, and AI agreement with physician electrocardiogram (ECG) interpretation. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from January 2010 through March 10, 2025. Bivariate random-effects models generated pooled sensitivity, specificity, and hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (AUC). Twenty-six studies comprising 539,876 ECGs were included. In 20 studies comparing AI with a clinical reference standard, pooled sensitivity was 0.95 (95% confidence interval, 0.91-0.97), specificity 0.95 (0.90-0.98), AUC 0.98 (0.97-0.99), positive likelihood ratio 19.2 (9.3-39.5), and negative likelihood ratio 0.05 (0.03-0.10). In 8 studies reporting both AI and clinician performance against a clinical reference, separate syntheses showed sensitivity of 0.91 (0.86-0.94) for AI versus 0.78 (0.69-0.85) for clinicians, specificity of 0.91 (0.82-0.96) for both, and AUCs of 0.95 and 0.90, respectively. In 7 studies using physician ECG interpretation as the comparator, AI sensitivity was 0.85 (0.70-0.94), specificity 0.99 (0.96-1.00), and AUC 0.98 (0.96-0.99). Sensitivity analyses excluding case-control designs, influential studies, and restricting analyses to deep learning models or raw waveform ECGs produced similar findings.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in the Management of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: A Narrative Review Informed by a Systematic Search.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in the Management of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: A Narrative Review Informed by a Systematic Search.
content.abstract:
Background

Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) remains a leading cause of mortality, and early identification of phenotypes, exacerbation risk, and treatment response remains challenging. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising tool for improving prediction, classification, and monitoring in COPD. This narrative review, informed by a systematic search, evaluated current AI applications in COPD management.

Methods

The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42024502765) and reported with reference to PRISMA 2020 principles. MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception to May 2025. Eligible studies applied Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, or Deep Learning approaches to adult COPD populations for diagnostic, prognostic, monitoring, phenotyping, or disease management purposes. Data extraction was performed independently by two reviewers, and methodological quality was appraised using design-appropriate tools.

Results

Twenty-two studies met the inclusion criteria. AI demonstrated high discriminative accuracy for COPD diagnosis, exacerbation prediction, and mortality risk (mean Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve [AUROC] = 0.83), although methodological heterogeneity and limited external validation were common. Models integrating multimodal data generally outperformed single-domain approaches. Risk-of-bias assessment identified concerns related to small sample sizes, limited external validation, and incomplete reporting of model development and validation procedures.

Conclusion

Current evidence suggests that AI may support COPD diagnosis, prognostic prediction, and telemonitoring. However, methodological heterogeneity, limited external validation, and inconsistent reporting standards continue to limit clinical translation. Further high-quality, externally validated studies are needed to support implementation in respiratory care.

records.title: Multimodal Carotid Ultrasound-based Artificial Intelligence Model for Predicting Acute Ischemic Stroke Risk in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.

content.title: Multimodal Carotid Ultrasound-based Artificial Intelligence Model for Predicting Acute Ischemic Stroke Risk in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
content.abstract:
Rationale and objectives
